verses.hebrew: בִּימֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ – הוּא אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ שֶׁמָּלַךְ מֵהוֹדּוּ וְעַד כּוּשׁ – עַל מֵאָה עֶשְׂרִים וְשֶׁבַע מְדִינוֹת.
verses.english: Once upon a time, in the days of a commoner called Ahasuerus.He married Vashti, a scion of the powerful Babylonian conqueror Nebuchadnezzar, and thereby suddenly became King Ahasuerus, the ruler of a vast empire – of one hundred and twenty-seven provinces – from India in the East to North-West Africa in the West.

verses.hebrew: בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם כְּשֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ מָלַךְ וְיָשַׁב עַל כִּסֵּא מַלְכוּתוֹ שֶׁבְּשׁוּשַׁן הַבִּירָה,
verses.english: It happened in those early days, when King Ahasuerus ascended his very own royal throne which he had audaciously relocated in his new capital city, the Shushan fortress, to display his individual might and disdain for the royal tradition.

verses.hebrew: בַּשָּׁנָה הַשְּׁלִישִׁית לְמַלְכוּתוֹ הוּא עָשָׂה מְסִבַּת שְׁתִיַּת יַיִן לְכָל שָׂרָיו וַעֲבָדָיו: לִצְבָא פָּרַס וּמָדַי וְלַשַּׁלִּיטִים וְשָׂרֵי הַמְּדִינוֹת שֶׁבְּשִׁלְטוֹנוֹ.
verses.english: In the third year of his attempt to remodel the monarchy and transition from law-abiding king to above-the-law dictator, he made a banquet to further this cause.First and foremost, his banquet was for all his officials and courtiers, and members of the Persian and Median military. Then, he also invited the nobles and provincial officials that had previously held office.The hierarchical manner of these invitations was intended to make a powerful political statement: the lawmakers of the past were now the subdued and obedient subjects of Ahasuerus’ military rule.

verses.hebrew: הוּא הֶרְאָה בָּהּ אֶת עוֹשְׁרוֹ וְאֶת כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ וְאֶת חֲשִׁיבוּתוֹ וּפְאֵר גְּדוּלָּתוֹ, בְּמֶשֶׁךְ יָמִים רַבִּים – מֵאָה וּשְׁמוֹנִים יָמִים.
verses.english: Moreover, at this banquet, he flaunted the national treasures as though they were his own. He presented them as personal wealth befitting his honourable kingship, and lavishness befitting his magnificent greatness. He brazenly did this for many days – one hundred and eighty in total.

verses.hebrew: וּכְשֶׁעָבְרוּ הַיָּמִים הָאֵלֶּה, הַמֶּלֶךְ עָשָׂה מְסִבַּת שְׁתִיַּת יַיִן שִׁבְעָה יָמִים, לְכָל הָעָם שֶׁנִּמְצְאִים בְּשׁוּשַׁן הַבִּירָה מִגָּדוֹל וְעַד קָטָן בֶּחָצֵר שֶׁל גִּנַּת אַרְמוֹן הַמֶּלֶךְ.
verses.english: After successfully completing these one hundred and eighty days of festivities, the king made a further seven-day banquet for all the common folk that lived in the environs of the Shushan fortress, from the highest-ranking to lowest-ranking. He held it in the courtyard of the king’s palatial gardens, where no commoner had previously been permitted to set foot. He did this to further demonstrate his disdain for tradition and convention, along with his disregard for the privileges the nobility had hitherto enjoyed.

verses.hebrew: יְרִיעוֹת בְּלָבָן וִירַקְרַק וּתְכֵלֶת קְשׁוּרוֹת בְּחַבְלֵי פִשְׁתָּן וְאַרְגָּמָן עַל וָוֵי כֶּסֶף וְעַמּוּדֵי שַׁיִשׁ, וְיָשְׁבוּ עַל מִטּוֹת שֶׁל זָהָב וָכֶסֶף עַל רִצְפָּה מֵאַבְנֵי הַחֵן בַּהַט וְשַׁיִשׁ וְדַר וְסוֹחָרֶת.
verses.english: For this banquet, he constructed a most extravagant marquee: It had tenting of white and indigo-blue cotton that was held in place by ropes of fine linen and purple and supported by silver cylinders and alabaster columns. It was furnished with couches of silver and gold, laid out on flooring of marble, alabaster, mother-of-pearl, and mosaic.

verses.hebrew: וּשְׁתִיָּה בִּכְלֵי זָהָב וְכֵלִים מִסּוּגִים שׁוֹנִים, וְהַרְבֵּה יַיִן מַלְכוּתִי – כְּיַד הַמֶּלֶךְ.
verses.english: And the drinks were served in sets of golden vessels, of which there were so many that each guest received his own set. And there was a vast supply of delicious wine that was fit for a king, as befits a king’s financial ability.

verses.hebrew: וְהַשְּׁתִיָּה כְּמוֹ שֶׁרְגִילִים – אֵין חוֹבָה לִשְׁתּוֹת, כִּי כָּךְ צִוָּה הַמֶּלֶךְ עַל כָּל הָאַחְרָאִים בְּבֵיתוֹ – לַעֲשׂוֹת כִּרְצוֹן כָּל אִישׁ.
verses.english: To further upend the stature of the nobility, he dispensed with the customary toasts: The drinking policy was that nobody should be forced to toast to his superiors, for this was the king’s instruction to all the important members of his court: “Let each man behave as he pleases”.

verses.hebrew: גַּם וַשְׁתִּי הַמַּלְכָּה עָשְׂתָה מְסִבַּת שְׁתִיַּת יַיִן לַנָּשִׁים בְּאַרְמוֹן הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ.
verses.english: To demonstrate that Queen Vashti was queen by virtue of being his wife, rather than him being king by virtue of being her husband, she also made a banquet, but only for the women, and she was made to hold it in the royal quarters that belonged to King Ahasuerus, rather than in her own quarters.

verses.hebrew: בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי, כְּשֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ שָׂמַח בַּיַּיִן, הוּא אָמַר לִמְהוּמָן, בִּזְּתָא, חַרְבוֹנָא, בִּגְתָא וַאֲבַגְתָא, זֵתַר וְכַרְכַּס – שִׁבְעַת הַמְּשָׁרְתִים שֶׁלִּפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ,
verses.english: Moreover, on the seventh and final day of the banquet, when the king was merry with wine, he decided to publicly exhibit that he had only married Vashti for her good looks and had no regard for her royal lineage. And so, he instructed Mehuman, Bizzeta, Charvona, Bigta, Avagta, Zetar, and Charcas, the seven valets who were the personal attendants of King Ahasuerus –

verses.hebrew: לְהָבִיא אֶת וַשְׁתִּי הַמַּלְכָּה לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ בְּכֶתֶר מַלְכוּת, כְּדֵי לְהַרְאוֹת לָעַמִּים וְלַשָּׂרִים אֶת יָפְיָהּ שֶׁהִיא נִרְאֵית טוֹב.
verses.english: To bring Vashti the Queen to stand before the king, and then place the crown on her head in his presence. This was intended to show the nations and the officials that she was only queen by virtue of being his wife, and that he had chosen her as his wife solely because she was beautiful, for indeed she was very good looking.Through this blatant act of disparaging the royal family into which he had married, Ahasuerus hoped to unequivocally demonstrate to his subjects that he had broken with past conventions. From now on, he would autonomously determine policy without restraint.But Vashti felt entitled to be the queen by virtue of her royal lineage, and so she refused to come. She refused to belittle herself by obeying the king’s disrespectful command, and to submit herself to being handled by his lowly valets rather than her personal chambermaids.

verses.hebrew: הַמַּלְכָּה וַשְׁתִּי סֵרְבָה לָבוֹא כִּפְקֻדַּת הַמֶּלֶךְ שֶׁנִּמְסְרָה עַל יְדֵי הַמְּשָׁרְתִים, הַמֶּלֶךְ הִתְרַגֵּז מְאוֹד וְכַעֲסוֹ בָּעַר בּוֹ.
verses.english: The king was outwardly furious that she had publicly humiliated him, and inwardly aggrieved that she had ruined his politically-motivated exhibition.

verses.hebrew: הַמֶּלֶךְ דִּבֵּר עִם הַחֲכָמִים שֶׁמְּבִינִים בְּאַסְטְרוֹלוֹגְיָה, כִּי כָּךְ מִנְהַג הַמֶּלֶךְ בְּמִשְׁפָּט – לְהִתְיַעֵץ עִם כָּל יוֹדְעֵי הַחֻקִּים וְהַדִּינִים.
verses.english: However, the king loved her dearly and wished to spare her from punishment. And so the king informed the wise fellows of the royal court assigned to her trial, who combined legal expertise with an appreciation of contextual factors, that although this case involves slighting the king, it was a marital feud that could just as well be heard by any commoners’ court that appreciates morality as well as law.

verses.hebrew: וְהַמְּקוֹרָבִים אֵלָיו הָיוּ: כַּרְשְׁנָא, שֵׁתָר, אַדְמָתָא, תַּרְשִׁישׁ, מֶרֶס, מַרְסְנָא וּמְמוּכָן – שִׁבְעַת שָׂרֵי פָּרַס וּמָדַי רוֹאֵי פְּנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ שֶׁיּוֹשְׁבִים רִאשׁוֹנִים בִּישִׁיבוֹת הַמַּלְכוּת.
verses.english: Matters were eased by the fact that he was well acquainted with the judges assigned to the case. Their names were Carshena, Shetar, Admata, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memuchan. They were the seven officials of Persia and Media who frequently saw the king, with the foremost experience in the royal court.He therefore hoped that they would cooperate with his attempts to secure Vashti’s acquittal and hush up the case.

verses.hebrew: שָׁאַל אוֹתָם הַמֶּלֶךְ: מַה לְפִי הַחוֹק צָּרִיךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת לַמַּלְכָּה וַשְׁתִּי עַל כָּךְ שֶׁלֹּא עָשְׂתָה אֶת פְּקֻדַּת הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ שֶׁמָּסַר לָהּ עַל יְדֵי הַמְּשָׁרְתִים?
verses.english: He emphasized that he sought a morally sensitive ruling on how to respond to Queen Vashti who was herself a royal, and had perhaps only disobeyed King Ahasuerus’ order because it had been disrespectfully sent in the hands of his valets.

verses.hebrew: אָמַר מְמוּכָן לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ וְהַשָּׂרִים: לֹא רַק כְּלַפֵּי הַמֶּלֶךְ פָּשְׁעָה וַשְׁתִּי הַמַּלְכָּה, אֶלָּא גַּם כְּלַפֵּי כָּל הַשָּׂרִים וְכָל הָעַמִּים שֶׁבְּכָל מְדִינוֹת הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ.
verses.english: However, much to the king’s dismay, Memuchan loudly proclaimed in the presence of the king and the officials that Vashti’s crime could not be hushed up, because her disobedience was far more serious than a commoner’s marital feud. Firstly, he argued that Vashti was only the queen by virtue of being Ahasuerus’ wife – her noncompliance risked derailing the king’s ambitions to cement his dictatorship. Secondly, he argued that she did not only commit an offense against the king, but also against all the officials and all the peoples in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus – she set a terrible precedent for all women throughout the empire.

verses.hebrew: כִּי כְּשֶׁהַסִּפּוּר עִם הַמַּלְכָּה יִתְפַּרְסֵם אֵצֶל כָּל הַנָּשִׁים בַּעְלֵיהֶן יִתְבַּזּוּ בְּעֵינֵיהֶן, וְהֵן יֹאמְרוּ: אֲפִלּוּ הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ אָמַר לְהָבִיא לְפָנָיו אֶת וַשְׁתִּי הַמַּלְכָּה וְהִיא לֹא בָּאָה!
verses.english: How so? Because word of the queen’s behavior will spread amongst all the women throughout the empire, and will cause them to view their husbands with condescension. Because they will reason: If King Ahasuerus commanded that Queen Vashti merely be brought before him, and yet she was defiant and would not come, all the more so ought we to defy our commoner husbands’ tough and unreasonable demands!The masses will interpret Vashti’s behaviour as a simple act of feminine defiance, since they will fail to realize the political significance of Vashti’s refusal.

verses.hebrew: וּמֵהַיּוֹם שָׂרוֹת פָּרַס וּמָדַי שֶׁשָּׁמְעוּ אֶת הַסִּפּוּר עִם הַמַּלְכָּה יֹאמְרוּ כָּךְ גַּם לְכָל שָׂרֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ, וְזֶה יִגְרוֹם לְהַרְבֵּה בִּזָּיוֹן וְכַעַס.
verses.english: And because already today the court ladies of Persia and Media who heard the queen’s outburst will relay news of her political defiance to all the king’s officials, and there will be enormous disgrace and outcry! The nobility will realize that Ahasuerus’ dictatorial ambitions are contested even within his own palace.

verses.hebrew: לָכֵן, אִם זֶה טוֹב בְּעֵינֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ, יֵצֵא צַו מַלְכוּתִי מִלְּפָנָיו וְיִכָּתֵב בְּסֵפֶר חֻקֵּי פָּרַס וּמָדַי חוֹק שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁתַּנֶּה, שֶׁוַּשְׁתִּי לֹא תָּבוֹא יוֹתֵר לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ, וְהַמֶּלֶךְ יִתֵּן אֶת מַלְכוּתָהּ לְאִשָּׁה אַחֶרֶת טוֹבָה מִמֶּנָּה.
verses.english: But do not worry! I have a plan to right these two wrongs; to salvage the king’s dictatorial ambitions and to reassert male authority among the commoner masses.If it seems good to the king, from now on all governmental directives should be personally issued by him, and codified, for eternity, in the legal traditions of Persia and Media. From now on, the king shall formally reside above the law; he shall become the empire’s supreme lawmaker.Then, the king should utilize his new powers and decree that Vashti shall never again appear before King Ahasuerus.Finally, the king should hand over her royal title to a commoner who is more desirable as a woman than her. Find a new wife, and emphasize character and beauty over lineage and bloodline. She will certainly be mindful of Vashti’s fate and treat you with the utmost respect, just as a good wife should.

verses.hebrew: וְהַדָּבָר הַזֶּה שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ יַעֲשֶׂה יִתְפַּרְסֵם בְּכָל מַמְלַכְתּוֹ – שֶׁהִיא גְּדוֹלָה, וְכָךְ כָּל הַנָּשִׁים יִתְּנוּ כָּבוֹד לְבַעְלֵיהֶן בֵּין אִם הוּא חָשׁוּב אוֹ פָּשׁוּט.
verses.english: If only the king will follow my counsel, from now on all legal directives advanced by the king will resound throughout the empire, because his monarchy shall stand supreme above the law. And all the women will treat their husbands with respect, be they high-ranking or low-ranking. Even women who married lower-ranking men than themselves will think twice after learning of the venerable Vashti’s fate.

verses.hebrew: הָרַעְיוֹן נִרְאָה טוֹב בְּעֵינֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ וְהַשָּׂרִים, וְהַמֶּלֶךְ עָשָׂה כְּדִבְרֵי מְמוּכָן.
verses.english: And this seemed like a good plan in the eyes of the king and his inner circle of officials. The king then autonomously implemented Memuchan’s plan.Thus the revolution was formalized; the seven top governmental officials resigned their legislative powers to the king who immediately acted upon them.

verses.hebrew: הוּא שָׁלַח מִכְתָּבִים אֶל כָּל מְדִינוֹת הַמֶּלֶךְ – אֶל כָּל מְדִינָה וּמְדִינָה בִּכְתָבָהּ וְאֶל כָּל עָם וְעָם בִּשְׂפָתוֹ, שֶׁכָּל אִישׁ יִשְׁלוֹט בְּבֵיתוֹ וִידַבֵּר בִּשְׁפַת עַמּוֹ וְלֹא בִּשְׁפַת אִשְׁתּוֹ.
verses.english: He dispatched legal scrolls, and addressed them to all the countries of “the king’s empire”. They were no longer to be known as the “Persian and Median empire”; the king had radically broken with the conventions of the past, and now they were accountable to him alone.Moreover, he had each country’s scroll written in its own alphabet, and each nation’s scroll in its own language. By not writing in the empire’s formal script and tongue, he further demonstrated his break with the past, and that from now on all his subjects were to be equally subjugated.The scrolls decreed that each man shall have dictatorial powers over his household whereas each woman shall be deprived of all rights. This edict attempted to counter the negative repercussions of Vashti’s behaviour.Moreover, they commanded that all formal communications with government shall now be conducted in one’s native language. This edict would be a constant reminder that the status quo of the “Persian and Median empire” had been abolished; from now on each country would be personally accountable to King Ahasuerus alone.

verses.hebrew: אַחֲרֵי הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה כְּשֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ אַחֲשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ נִרְגַּע מִכַּעֲסוֹ, הוּא נִזְכַּר בְּוַשְׁתִּי וּמַה שֶּׁעָשְׂתָה וּמַה שֶּׁנִּגְזַר עָלֶיהָ.
verses.english: Sometime later, when King Ahasuerus’ anger had been calmed, he remembered with longing his beautiful and influential Vashti, the nature of the offense she had committed, and the harsh consequences that were decreed on her.Realizing how unfairly and disproportionately she had been treated, he feared that no woman of Vashti’s calibre would dare enter into marriage with him.

verses.hebrew: הִצִּיעוּ לוֹ נַעֲרֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ מְשָׁרְתָיו: יְחַפְּשׂוּ לַמֶּלֶךְ נְעָרוֹת בְּתוּלוֹת יָפוֹת.
verses.english: When the king’s young menservants learned of his concerns, they said: Let the government issue a public appeal to provide the king with good-looking virgin young women.

verses.hebrew: וְהַמֶּלֶךְ יְמַנֶּה פְּקִידִים בְּכָל מְדִינוֹת מַלְכוּתוֹ, שֶׁיַּאַסְפוּ כָּל נַעֲרָה בְּתוּלָה יָפָה לְשׁוּשַׁן הַבִּירָה לְבֵית הַנָּשִׁים שֶׁבְּנִיהוּל הֵגֶא שַׂר הַמֶּלֶךְ שׁוֹמֵר הַנָּשִׁים, וְיִתְנוּ לָהֶם תַּמְרוּקִים.
verses.english: And should the young women fail to come forward of their own accord, the king can appoint administrators in each province of his empire, and they can forcibly gather all the good-looking virgin young women and transport them to the harem located in the Shushan fortress.To train their obedience and ensure that they do not become arrogant, they shall be tended to by a simple male valet, Hegai – caretaker of the women. They shall not be permitted to travel with their own cosmetics. Rather, these shall be handed to them by the palace staff to reward good behaviour.

verses.hebrew: וְהַנַּעֲרָה שֶׁתִּמְצָא חֵן בְּעֵינֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ תִּמְלוֹךְ בִּמְקוֹם וַשְׁתִּי. הָרַעֲיוֹן מָצָא חֵן בְּעֵינֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ, וְכָךְ הוּא עָשָׂה.
verses.english: And the young woman who seems worthy in the eyes of the king shall become queen in Vashti’s stead!It seemed like a good plan to the king, and so he autonomously enacted the relevant policy using his newfound legislative powers.

verses.hebrew: בְּשׁוּשַׁן הַבִּירָה הָיָה אִישׁ מֵאֶרֶץ יְהוּדָה וּשְׁמוֹ מָרְדֳּכַי בֶּן יָאִיר בֶּן שִׁמְעִי בֶּן קִישׁ, מִשֵׁבֶט בִּנְיָמִין.
verses.english: Now, there was a brave and righteous Jewish man who had lived for some time in the Shushan fortress. His name was Mordechai and he enjoyed royal ancestry; he was the son of Ya’ir, who was son of Shimi, who was son of Kish – the famed father of King Sha’ul – of the tribe of Binyamin.

verses.hebrew: הוּא הֻגְלָה מִיְּרוּשָׁלַיִם עִם הַגּוֹלָה שֶׁהֻגְלְתָה עִם יְכָנְיָה מֶלֶךְ יְהוּדָה, שֶׁהֶגְלָה אוֹתָהּ נְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּר מֶלֶךְ בָּבֶל.
verses.english: He had been deported from Jerusalem, among the upper class, lawmaker and artisan deportees that were deported along with Yechanyah, King of Judea. They were deported by Nebuchadnezzar, King of Babylonia.As a member of the Jewish upper class, a refugee, and a resident of Shushan who lived right near government headquarters, Mordechai had no excuse – neither unworthiness, privilege, or ignorance – to believe that his family was exempt from the king’s edict.But, motivated by his religious faith and contempt for the crass royal court, he did his best to conceal Esther –

verses.hebrew: הוּא אִמֵּץ אֶת הֲדַסָּה – הִיא אֶסְתֵּר בַּת דּוֹדוֹ, כִּי לֹא הָיָה לָהּ אָב וָאֵם, וְהַנַּעֲרָה יָפָה בְּצוּרַת גּוּפָהּ וְנִרְאֵית טוֹב, וּכְשֶׁמֵּתוּ אָבִיהָ וְאִמָּהּ לָקַח אוֹתָהּ מָרְדֳּכַי אֵלָיו וְאִמֵּץ אוֹתָהּ כְּבַת.
verses.english: He was the legal guardian of his cousin, whom he had adopted as a daughter when her mother and father died. She was fondly known to all as Hadassah – a fragrant myrtle by virtue of her good deeds, but her real name was Esther. And the young woman had a beautiful figure and was good looking.

verses.hebrew: וּכְשֶׁהִתְפַּרְסֵם צַו הַמֶּלֶךְ וּגְזֵרָתוֹ וְנֶאֶסְפוּ נְעָרוֹת רַבּוֹת אֶל שׁוּשַׁן הַבִּירָה אֶל הֵגַי, אֶסְתֵּר נִלְקְחָה אֶל בֵּית הַמֶּלֶךְ אֶל הֵגַי שׁוֹמֵר הַנָּשִׁים.
verses.english: And it came to be, when the king pronounced his alluring words to tempt the young women to come forth willingly and then, due to their ineffectiveness, followed this with his decree insisting that they be sent, that many young women were made to gather in the Shushan fortress subject to the care of Hegai. Then, Esther too was forcibly taken to the king’s palace, subject to the care of Hegai the caretaker of the women.

verses.hebrew: הַנַּעֲרָה מָצְאָה חֵן בְּעֵינָיו וְהוּא חִבֵּב אוֹתָהּ, הוּא מִהֵר לָתֵת לָהּ אֶת תַּמְרוּקֶיהָ וְאֶת מְנוֹת הָאוֹכֶל שֶׁלָּהּ, וְאֶת שֶׁבַע הַמְּשָׁרְתוֹת שֶׁהִיא אֲמוּרָה לְקַבֵּל מִבֵּית הַמֶּלֶךְ, וְהוּא הִפְלָה לְטוֹבָה אוֹתָהּ וְאֶת נַעֲרוֹתֶיהָ בְּבֵית הַנָּשִׁים.
verses.english: But although Esther had defied the king’s orders and attempted to escape his clutches, she was not punished by Hegai, because the young woman seemed to be the ideal candidate in his eyes, and so she found favour before him and he forgave her.He was so confident that she would be the next queen that he hastily ordered her cosmetic treatments and provisions, and even summoned a team of seven chambermaids from the king’s palace to tend to her needs, that would befit her once she became queen. And she and her chambermaids received differential treatment in the finest quarters of the harem.

verses.hebrew: אֶסְתֵּר לֹא סִפְּרָה מַהוּ עַמָּהּ וְאֵיפֹה נוֹלְדָה כִּי מָרְדֳּכַי צִוָּה עָלֶיהָ שֶׁלֹּא תְּסַפֵּר.
verses.english: Despite being singled out in this way, Esther would not share her national and familial identity, because Mordechai had instructed her not to share it. They hoped that Esther’s avoidance of discussing her lineage would lead the officials to presume she was a bastard and expel her from the harem.

verses.hebrew: וּבְכָל יוֹם מָרְדֳּכַי מִתְהַלֵּךְ לִפְנֵי חֲצַר בֵּית הַנָּשִׁים כְּדֵי לָדַעַת מַה שְּׁלוֹם אֶסְתֵּר וּמַה עוֹשִׂים אִתָּהּ.
verses.english: But this strategy also risked antagonizing the court, and Mordechai was concerned that Esther’s concerted efforts to avoid the king would be viewed as treasonous and severely punished. And so, every single day Mordechai would walk about in front of the court of the harem, to learn of Esther’s wellbeing and what they intended to do with her. Thankfully, Esther’s charm stood her in good stead, and she survived unscathed.

verses.hebrew: כְּשֶׁמַּגִּיעַ תּוֹר כָּל נַעֲרָה לָבוֹא אֶל הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ, כְּשֶׁמִּסְתַּיְּמִים שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר הֶחֳדָשִׁים שֶׁל הִתְקַשְּׁטוּת כְּמִנְהַג הַנָּשִׁים, כִּי כָּךְ זְמַן הַהִתְמָרְקוּת בַּבְּשָׂמִים – שִׁשָּׁה חֳדָשִׁים בְּשֶׁמֶן מוֹר וְשִׁשָּׁה חֳדָשִׁים בִּבְשָׂמִים וּבְתַמְרוּקֵי נָשִׁים.
verses.english: When each young woman’s turn came to go to King Ahasuerus – this would take place following her successful completion of a twelve month probation period prescribed for the women to ensure that they were healthy and not susceptible to any seasonal sicknesses, neither throughout the six cold months when they would warm themselves with oil of myrrh, nor throughout the six hot months when they would mask unpleasant body odours with perfumes and women’s cosmetics –

verses.hebrew: עִם זֶה הַנַּעֲרָה בָּאָה אֶל הַמֶּלֶךְ: כָּל מַה שֶׁתְּבַקֵּשׁ יִנָּתֵן לָהּ לָבוֹא אִתָּהּ מִבֵּית הַנָּשִׁים לְבֵית הַמֶּלֶךְ.
verses.english: With this alone – beauty, trained obedience and a statement of clean health – the young woman would go to the king, because there were no other virtues that he deemed pertinent. Moreover, to encourage consensualness and agreeableness, she would be granted whatever she requested to bring along with her, during her transfer from the harem to the royal palace to commence her life as the king’s mistress.

verses.hebrew: בָּעֶרֶב הִיא בָּאָה, וּבַבּוֹקֶר הִיא חוֹזֶרֶת אֶל בֵּית הַנָּשִׁים הַשֵּׁנִי אֶל שַׁעַשְׁגַז שַׂר הַמֶּלֶךְ שׁוֹמֵר הַפִּילַגְשִׁים, הִיא לֹא תָּבוֹא שׁוּב אֶל הַמֶּלֶךְ אֶלָּא אִם הַמֶּלֶךְ יִרְצֶה אוֹתָהּ וְיִקְרָא בִּשְׁמָהּ.
verses.english: And thus, the young woman went willingly even though her moment in the spotlight was short-lived. She would arrive in the evening and return in the morning to a second harem under the care of Sha’ashgaz, the king’s valet, caretaker of the concubines. She would not have a further opportunity to go to the king unless he desired her, whereupon she would be summoned by name.

verses.hebrew: וּכְשֶׁהִגִּיעַ הַתּוֹר שֶׁל אֶסְתֵּר בַּת אֲבִיחַיִל הַדּוֹד שֶׁל מָרְדֳּכַי שֶׁאִמֵּץ אוֹתָהּ כְּבַת, לָבוֹא אֶל הַמֶּלֶךְ, הִיא לֹא בִּקְשָׁה שׁוּם דָּבָר אֶלָּא רַק אֶת מַה שֶּׁיֹּאמַר הֵגַי מְשָׁרֵת הַמֶּלֶךְ שׁוֹמֵר הַנָּשִׁים. אֶסְתֵּר מָצְאָה חֵן בְּעֵינֵי כָּל רוֹאֶיהָ.
verses.english: But when the turn of Esther, the daughter of Avichayil, the uncle of Mordechai – who had subsequently adopted her as his daughter – came to go to the king, she did things differently. She requested no gifts to clearly communicate that she did not consent. She only took what Hegai the king’s valet and caretaker of the women personally instructed her to take. But, once again, due to her unique combination of beauty with refinement of character and intellect imbibed from her childhood home, Esther’s defiance went unpunished. On the contrary, she won the admiration of all who saw her.

verses.hebrew: אֶסְתֵּר נִלְקְחָה אֶל הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ אֶל בֵּית מַלְכוּתוֹ בַּחוֹדֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂירִי הוּא חוֹדֶשׁ טֵבֵת בַּשָּׁנָה הַשְּׁבִיעִית לְמַלְכוּתוֹ.
verses.english: And Esther had to be taken by force to King Ahasuerus, transported to his quarters within the palace. This took place in the tenth month – the month of Tevet, in the seventh year of his reign.

verses.hebrew: הַמֶּלֶךְ אָהַב אֶת אֶסְתֵּר יוֹתֵר מִכָּל הַנָּשִׁים, וְהִיא מָצְאָה חֵן וְהָיְתָה חֲבִיבָה בְּעֵינָיו יוֹתֵר מִכָּל הַבְּתוּלוֹת, הוּא שָׂם כֶּתֶר מַלְכוּת עַל רֹאשָׁהּ וְהִמְלִיךְ אוֹתָהּ בִּמְקוֹם וַשְׁתִּי.
verses.english: And the king loved Esther more than all the women he had met, and he admired her and felt more kindly toward her than to all the other virgin candidates. And so, without further ado, he personally placed the royal crown on her head and appointed her queen in Vashti’s stead.

verses.hebrew: הַמֶּלֶךְ עָשָׂה מְסִבַּת שְׁתִיַּת יַיִן גְּדוֹלָה לְכָל שָׂרָיו וַעֲבָדָיו לִכְבוֹד אֶסְתֵּר, וְהוּא עָשָׂה הֲנָחָה לַמְּדִינוֹת בְּתַשְׁלוּם הַמִּסִּים, וְנָתַן מַתָּנוֹת כְּיַד הַמֶּלֶךְ.
verses.english: Esther’s secretiveness regarding her identity fascinated the king. He was consumed with curiosity, and attempted to cajole her into revealing it. To this end, the king threw a great banquet for all his officials and courtiers and called it “the banquet of Esther.” He hoped that she would be embarrassed to present herself to the adoring public as an identity-less bastard. He also proclaimed tax remissions for the provinces and distributed gifts as befits a king. He hoped that she would be tempted to reveal at least her national identity in order to take full advantage of the king’s generosity and secure a good package for her people.

verses.hebrew: גַּם כְּשֶׁאָסְפוּ בְּתוּלוֹת בְּפַעַם שְׁנִיָּה, מָרְדֳּכַי הָיָה יוֹשֵׁב בְּשַׁעַר הַמֶּלֶךְ,
verses.english: Upon seeing that Esther would not yield, he hypothesized that underlying anxiety was at play. Perhaps she feared that disclosing an undesirable identity would lead the king to search for another wife. So, he arranged that the virgin young women were rounded up for a second time – this time from their quarters in the harem – and sent home. Now Esther had nothing to fear.Moreover, Mordechai – her adoptive parent – was appointed to sit in the king’s court that was located near the royal gates. Hopefully, Esther would reveal her identity to secure even better privileges for Mordechai.

verses.hebrew: וְאֶסְתֵּר לֹא סִפְּרָה אֵיפֹה נוֹלְדָה וּמַהוּ עַמָּהּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁצִּוָּה עָלֶיהָ מָרְדֳּכַי, אֶסְתֵּר מִלְּאָה אֶת הַהוֹרָאוֹת שֶׁל מָרְדֳּכַי כְּמוֹ בַּזְּמָן שֶׁהָיְתָה מְאֻמֶּצֶת אֶצְלוֹ.
verses.english: But, all his attempts were in vain. Esther would not reveal her family or national identity, just as Mordechai had instructed her; because Esther followed Mordechai’s opinion as she had done while living with him as an adoptee.Esther held her sage uncle in such esteem, that she willingly embraced risk to heed his bidding.

verses.hebrew: בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם שֶׁמָּרְדֳּכַי הָיָה יוֹשֵׁב בְּשַׁעַר הַמֶּלֶךְ כַּעֲסוּ בִּגְתָן וְתֶרֶשׁ שְׁנֵי מְשָׁרְתֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ מִשּׁוֹמְרֵי הַפֶּתַח, וְרָצוּ לְהִתְנַקֵּשׁ בַּמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ.
verses.english: How providential that precisely around this time, Mordechai was fulfilling his new role and sitting at the royal gates, when Bigtan and Teresh – two of the king’s valets tasked with guarding the threshold to his quarters – outwardly expressed their fury with the king to one another, and plotted to attack King Ahasuerus.

verses.hebrew: הַדָּבָר נוֹדַע לְמָרְדֳּכַי וְהוּא סִפֵּר לְאֶסְתֵּר הַמַּלְכָּה, וְאֶסְתֵּר אָמְרָה לַמֶּלֶךְ בְּשֵׁם מָרְדֳּכָי.
verses.english: But, being in the right place at the right time, the plot became known to Mordechai, and he relayed it to Queen Esther. Esther then informed the king in the name of Mordechai.

verses.hebrew: חָקְרוּ אֶת הַדָּבָר וְהוּא הִתְגַּלָּה, וּשְׁנֵיהֶם נִתְלוּ עַל עֵץ, וְזֶה נִכְתַּב בְּיוֹמַן הַזִּכְרוֹנוֹת שֶׁלִּפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ.
verses.english: The poisonous substance was sought and discovered, and they were both indicted of attempt to murder the king and hanged on a stake.Providentially, this episode was recorded in the king’s private diary rather in the formal royal chronicles, where it would likely have been erased by Haman. Providentially, the king chose to record Mordechai’s favor rather than repay it immediately, which would stand Mordechai and the Jewish people in good stead, as events unfold. And, how providential that only once the infrastructure for the Jew’s ultimate salvation was firmly in place – in the form of Esther and Mordechai’s relationships with the king – did Haman rise to power and endeavour to harm them.

verses.hebrew: אַחֲרֵי הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה, הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ רוֹמֵם אֶת הָמָן בֶּן הַמְּדָתָא הַצֶּאֱצָא שֶׁל אֲגָג, וְכִבֵּד אוֹתוֹ, וְקָבַע אֶת הַדַּרְגָּה שֶׁלּוֹ מֵעַל כָּל הַשָּׂרִים שֶׁאֶצְלוֹ.
verses.english: Sometime after the previous events, King Ahasuerus successively promoted Haman son of Hammedata the Agagite. He ultimately offered him the loftiest position in his government and placed his chair higher than those of all his fellow officials.

verses.hebrew: וְכָל עַבְדֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ שֶׁבְּשַׁעַר הַמֶּלֶךְ כּוֹרְעִים וּמִשְׁתַּחֲוִים לְהָמָן כִּי כָּךְ צִוָּה הַמֶּלֶךְ, וּמָרְדֳּכַי לֹא הָיָה כּוֹרֵע וְלֹא מִשְׁתַּחֲוֶה.
verses.english: The grandeur got to Haman’s head and he came to view himself as a demigod. Due to his insistence, all the king’s courtiers, even those working within the palace gates, would kneel and prostrate before Haman, because he had the king order this on his behalf. But Mordechai would not kneel or prostrate. As a Jewish leader, he thought it religiously unacceptable to honour a demigod in this manner.

verses.hebrew: עַבְדֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ שֶׁבְּשַׁעַר הַמֶּלֶךְ אָמְרוּ לְמָרְדֳּכָי: מַדּוּעַ אַתָּה עוֹבֵר עַל מִצְוַת הַמֶּלֶךְ?
verses.english: The courtiers of the king that were situated at the royal gates and tasked with enforcing this new law admonished Mordechai: “Why do you violate the king’s command?” But Mordechai stuck to his principles and disobeyed them.

verses.hebrew: הֵם הָיוּ אוֹמְרִים לוֹ כָּל יוֹם וְהוּא לֹא הִקְשִׁיב לָהֶם, הֵם סִפְּרוּ לְהָמָן כְּדֵי לִרְאוֹת אִם דִּבְרֵי מָרְדֳּכַי יַחֲזִיקוּ מַעֲמָד, כִּי הוּא הִסְבִּיר לָהֶם שֶׁאֵינוֹ כּוֹרֵעַ כִּי הוּא יְהוּדִי.
verses.english: One day, when their patience wore thin after admonishing him day after day while he continued to disobey them – citing his Jewishness as the reason – they informed Haman, and requested that he overtly visit Mordechai to see whether Mordechai’s excuse was valid.They reasoned that Mordechai’s Jewish sensitivities would not forbid bowing to Haman’s face, despite his demigod status, since it is universal etiquette to bow before all officials. If Mordechai would not bow even to Haman’s face, this would confirm that he was in contempt of the law.

verses.hebrew: הָמָן רָאָה שֶׁמָרְדֳּכַי אֵינוֹ כּוֹרֵעַ וּמִשְׁתַּחֲוֶה לוֹ וְהוּא הִתְמַלֵּא בְּכַעַס.
verses.english: And Haman visited Mordechai and saw that Mordechai still would not kneel or prostrate himself before him. Clearly, invoking Judaism had been a decoy; in fact, Mordechai refused to humble himself before Haman! Haman was too arrogant to show his affront outwardly, but inwardly he was filled with rage, and became bent on avenging his wounded pride.

verses.hebrew: הָיָה בָּזוּי בְּעֵינָיו לִפְגּוֹעַ רַק בְּמָרְדֳּכַי כִּי סִפְּרוּ לוֹ מִי הָעָם שֶׁל מָרְדֳּכָי, הָמָן רָצָה לְהַשְׁמִיד אֶת כָּל הַיְּהוּדִים – הָעָם שֶׁל מָרְדֳּכָי, שֶׁבְּכָל מַלְכוּת אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ.
verses.english: Although Haman had been personally affronted by Mordechai, the possibility of laying hands on Mordechai alone seemed pathetic in his eyes. It was beneath his dignity to take some Jew’s disrespectful behaviour to heart.So, given that he had originally been told about, and displeased by, the religious grounds for Mordechai’s refusal to bow before him, and that these were shared by his entire people, Haman plotted to destroy all the Jews throughout the kingdom of Ahasuerus, because they were Mordechai’s nation. They abided, like him, by such distasteful laws, and by ridding the empire of them, he would settle his score with Mordechai.

verses.hebrew: בַּחוֹדֶשׁ הָרִאשׁוֹן הוּא חוֹדֶשׁ נִיסָן, בִּשְׁנַת שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה לַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ הוּא עָשָׂה הַגְרָלָה, זֶה הַגּוֹרָל שֶׁעָשָׂה הָמָן, בְּאֵיזֶה יוֹם וּבְאֵיזֶה חוֹדֶשׁ, וְיָצָא הַחוֹדֶשׁ הַשְּׁנֵים עָשָׂר הוּא חוֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר.
verses.english: And so, shortly thereafter, in the first calendar month, that is, the month of Nisan, in the twelfth year of King Ahasuerus’ reign, the lot was cast before Haman who hoped that the very next day (the 14th) would be an auspicious day for executing his plot. But the lots dragged him from the next possible day (the 14th of Nisan) to the last possible day (the 13th of Iyar). Fearing that the entire coming month was not auspicious, Haman then cast lots to find the ideal month, but the lots dragged him from the first possible month (Nisan) to the last possible month, that is, the twelfth month, the month of Adar.

verses.hebrew: אָמַר הָמָן לַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ: יֵשׁ עַם אֶחָד מְפֻזָּר וּמְפוֹרָד בֵּין הָעַמִּים בְּכָל מְדִינוֹת מַמְלַכְתְּךָ, וְחֻקֵּיהֶם שׁוֹנִים מִשֶּׁל כָּל עָם, וְהֵם אֵינָם עוֹשִׂים אֶת חֻקֵּי הַמֶּלֶךְ, וְלַמֶּלֶךְ לֹא מִשְׁתַּלֵּם לְהַשְׁאִיר אוֹתָם.
verses.english: How providential that the lots literally fell on the latest possible date, buying the Jews maximum time.Unperturbed by this setback, Haman then went and said to King Ahasuerus: “There is ‘this people’, too insignificant to be named, that does not inhabit its own country or even its own cities, but is instead scattered and assimilated within the other nations throughout the provinces of your empire. Their religion has many doctrines that fundamentally differ from those of all other nations, and is thus a cultural anomaly. Moreover, they disobey the king’s laws even when not strictly required to do so on religious grounds. In this way, they corrode society and encourage civil unrest, and it is not worth the king’s while to let them be.

verses.hebrew: אִם זֶה רַעֲיוֹן טוֹב בְּעֵינֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ יִכָּתֵב צַו לְהַשְׁמִיד אוֹתָם, וְאֶשְׁקוֹל עֲשֶׂרֶת אֲלָפִים כִּכְּרוֹת כֶּסֶף וְאֶתֵּן לַמְּמוּנִים שֶׁיָּבִיאוּ אוֹתָם לְאוֹצַר הַמֶּלֶךְ.
verses.english: If it seems good in your eyes, I suggest that you have it written to neutralize them. This will be a simple and inexpensive project, and the taskforce will be so willing that I could raise ten thousand kikars of silver from them to invest in the king’s treasuries.”Haman hoped that his ambiguous terminology, “neutralize”, would be understood by Ahasuerus as cultural reformation and re-education policy. In fact, Haman held a far more sinister interpretation in mind – to neutralize them through genocide. As for the second half of his statement, while it contextually implied to Ahasuerus the willingness of the taskforce, Haman was in fact eyeing the vast loot of the massacred Jews and fantasizing of the plunder tax it would raise.

verses.hebrew: הַמֶּלֶךְ הֵסִיר אֶת טַבַּעַת הַחוֹתֶמֶת שֶׁלּוֹ מִיָּדוֹ וּמָסַר אוֹתָהּ לְהָמָן בֶּן הַמְּדָתָא הַצֶּאֱצָא שֶׁל אֲגָג, אוֹיֵב הַיְּהוּדִים.
verses.english: And indeed, the king fell prey to Haman’s ploy. He had no idea that Haman planned a genocide, and for a people no less significant than the Jews. So, the king removed his signet ring from his hand, and passed it to Haman son of Hammedata the Agagite, the foe of the Jews – scion of a famous Jew-hating family.

verses.hebrew: אָמַר הַמֶּלֶךְ לְהָמָן: הַכֶּסֶף נָתוּן לְךָ, וְגַם הָעָם – לַעֲשׂוֹת בּוֹ כִּרְצוֹנְךָ.
verses.english: Moreover, the king gratefully said to Haman, I will provide you with the necessary silver and you may act against this nation however you see fit.

verses.hebrew: סוֹפְרֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ הֻזְמְנוּ בְּי"ג לַחוֹדֶשׁ הָרִאשׁוֹן וְהֵם כָּתְבוּ אֶת כָּל מַה שֶּׁצִּוָּה הָמָן אֶל נְצִיבֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ וְאֶל הַמּוֹשְׁלִים שֶׁל כָּל מְדִינָה וּמְדִינָה וְאֶל שָׂרֵי כָּל עַם וְעַם, לְכָל מְדִינָה וּמְדִינָה בִּכְתָבָהּ וּלְכָל עָם וְעָם בִּשְׂפָתוֹ, נִכְתָּב בְּשֵׁם הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ וְנֶחְתָּם בְּחוֹתֶמֶת הַמֶּלֶךְ.
verses.english: And lest the king uncover his deception before it was too late, on that very day, on the thirteenth day of the first month - Nisan, the king’s scribes were summoned, and proclamations were written as per Haman’s instructions. They were addressed to the king’s satraps, and to the governors of every province, and to the officials of every nation. They wrote to every province in its own script and to every people in its own language, because typically, many dialects were spoken in each province, but all shared a script. The orders were issued in the name of King Ahasuerus and sealed with the king’s signet.

verses.hebrew: וְשָׁלְחוּ מִכְתָּבִים בִּידֵי הָרָצִים אֶל כָּל מְדִינוֹת הַמֶּלֶךְ, וְכָתוּב בָּהֶם לְהַשְׁמִיד לַהֲרוֹג וּלְאַבֵּד אֶת כָּל הַיְּהוּדִים מִנַּעַר וְעַד זָקֵן, יְלָדִים וְנָשִׁים, בְּיוֹם אֶחָד – בְּיוֹם י"ג לְחוֹדֶשׁ שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר הוּא חוֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר, וְלָקַחַת אֶת שְׁלָלָם.
verses.english: And, he immediately dispatched them as scrolls with the high-speed couriers to all the king’s provinces.And this is what they proclaimed: “To destroy, massacre, and neutralize all the Jews, from the young to the old, children and women, on a single day, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month – that is, the month of Adar – and to plunder their possessions.”Cunningly, he personalized each letter with script and language, to imply to its recipients that the decree only pertained to the Jews residing in that location. It was thus unlikely that individual communities would comprehend that this was part of an empire-wide genocide, which could lead them to dissent.

verses.hebrew: תּוֹכֶן הַמִּכְתָב: לִקְבּוֹעַ בְּכָל מְדִינָה חוֹק וּלְפַרְסֵם אֵצֶל כָּל הָעַמִּים, שֶׁיִּהְיוּ מוּכָנִים לַיּוֹם הַזֶּה.
verses.english: To further conceal his plot from the king, and from the Jews – who would rally to defend themselves if given ample advance notice, he sent a supplement to the sealed written edicts, that was to be legally enacted in each province and publicised among all the nations. It stated: “Be militarily prepared for that day – the 13th of Adar. But the scrolls themselves are not to be opened before the 13th of Adar”.In this way, nobody would know in advance that the Jews were the target.

verses.hebrew: הָרָצִים יָצְאוּ בִּדְחִיפוּת לַעֲשׂוֹת אֶת דְּבַר הַמֶּלֶךְ, וְנִקְבַּע הַחוֹק בְּשׁוּשַׁן הַבִּירָה, וְהַמֶּלֶךְ וְהָמָן יָשְׁבוּ לִשְׁתּוֹת יַיִן וּבָעִיר שׁוּשָׁן הָיוּ נְבוֹכִים.
verses.english: Finally, only once the high-speed couriers had been dispatched was the law enacted in the Shushan fortress lest the locals discover the plot and lobby the king to block it.Oblivious to the genocidal nature of the new law, the king sat with Haman to drink wine – which would have otherwise been culturally proscribed, since no one drank wine and sentenced to death on the same day.And the population of wider Shushan – beyond the fortress – was intrigued by the mysterious new decree.

verses.hebrew: וּמָרְדֳּכַי יָדַע אֶת כָּל מַה שֶׁקָּרָה, מָרְדֳּכַי קָרַע אֶת בְּגָדָיו וְלָבַשׁ בֶּגֶד גַּס מִשֵּׂעָר עִזִּים שְׁחוֹרוֹת וְשָׂם אֵפֶר עַל רֹאשׁוֹ, וְיָצָא בְּתוֹךְ הָעִיר וְזָעַק זְעָקָה גְּדוֹלָה וּמָרָה.
verses.english: Despite Haman’s efforts to conceal the Jewish genocide, Mordechai knew everything that had transpired. And Mordechai’s response began with humble repentance to G-d; he tore his clothes and donned sackcloth and ashes. Then he went through the city centre, and screamed loudly and bitterly, to draw attention to the evil decree and publicize its contents to the masses.

verses.hebrew: הוּא בָּא עַד לִפְנֵי שַׁעַר הַמֶּלֶךְ, כִּי אָסוּר לְהִכָּנֵס לְשַׁעַר הַמֶּלֶךְ בִּלְבוּשׁ גַּס.
verses.english: Then he went to publicize the decree in the palace, by making a scene as he approached the royal gate. But he did not enter through it, for one may not enter the royal gate wearing sackcloth.

verses.hebrew: וּבְכָל מְדִינָה וּמְדִינָה בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁפְּקֻדַּת הַמֶּלֶךְ וּגְזֵרָתוֹ מַגִּיעָה, אֵבֶל גָּדוֹל לַיְּהוּדִים וְצוֹם וּבְכִי וְקִינוֹת, וְרַבִּים שׁוֹכְבִים עַל בַּד גַּס מִשֵּׂעָר עִזִּים שְׁחוֹרוֹת וְעַל אֵפֶר.
verses.english: And as Mordechai had intended, the bitter news spread throughout the empire; it reached each province even if not each town and village.And, in those places in every province that news of the discrepancy between the king’s actual words and the text of Haman’s decree reached, there was great mourning among the Jews, with fasting, weeping, and lamenting; sackcloth and ashes were laid before the masses.Throughout the empire, the Jews repented and rallied around G-d.

verses.hebrew: נַעֲרוֹת אֶסְתֵּר וְהַמְּשָׁרְתִים שֶׁלָּהּ בָּאוּ וְסִפְּרוּ לָהּ וְהַמַּלְכָּה הִזְדַּעַזְעָה מְאוֹד, הִיא שָׁלְחָה בְּגָדִים לְהַלְבִּישׁ אֶת מָרְדֳּכַי וְשֶׁיָּסִיר אֶת הַבֶּגֶד הַגַּס מֵעָלָיו, וְהוּא לֹא הִסְכִּים לְקַבֵּל.
verses.english: Back at the palace, the chambermaids and valets of Esther came to inform her about Mordechai’s behaviour, and the Queen became very agitated. Immediately, she sent fresh clothes in which to dress Mordechai so that his sackcloth would not be externally visible. Then, he could enter the palace and explain the situation to her. However, he refused the clothing, lest dressing up for the court distract him – albeit momentarily – from his penitence.

verses.hebrew: אֶסְתֵּר קָרְאָה לַהֲתָךְ – אֶחָד מִשָּׂרֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ שֶׁהוּא הֶעֱמִיד לְשֵׁרוּתָהּ, הִיא צִוְּתָה עָלָיו לִשְׁאוֹל אֶת מָרְדֳּכָי כְּדֵי לָדַעַת מַה זֶּה וְעַל מַה זֶּה.
verses.english: Seeing that there was no way to bring Mordechai into the palace, Esther summoned Hatach, the valet that the king had assigned as her personal aide, and the member of the palace staff whom she trusted most.She instructed him to inquire about Mordechai’s behaviour and message, and to define for her what the problem was, and what its underlying causes were. She hoped to gather enough information to understand the nature of the issue, and how to go about fixing it.

verses.hebrew: הֲתָךְ יָצָא אֶל מָרְדֳּכָי אֶל רַחֲבַת הָעִיר שֶׁלִּפְנֵי שַׁעַר הַמֶּלֶךְ.
verses.english: And so Hatach went out to Mordechai, to the city square in front of the royal gate.

verses.hebrew: מָרְדֳּכַי סִפֵּר לוֹ אֶת כָּל מַה שֶּׁקָּרָה לוֹ בִּגְלַל שֶׁלֹּא הִשְׁתַּחֲוָה לְהָמָן, וְאֶת סְכוּם הַכֶּסֶף שֶׁהָמָן אָמַר שֶׁיָּבִיא לְאוֹצְרוֹת הַמֶּלֶךְ בִּשְׁבִיל לְהַשְׁמִיד אֶת הַיְּהוּדִים.
verses.english: Fortunately, Mordechai trusted him and told him directly everything he needed to know; how it all related to his personal encounters with Haman, where he had refused to bow to him. He also told him about the scandalous saga with the silver; how Haman had misled Ahasuerus with his ambiguous smooth talk, and in reality, offered to raise plunder taxation for the royal treasury for the right to “neutralize” the Jews.

verses.hebrew: וְנָתַן לוֹ עוֹתֶק מִכְּתַב הַחוֹק שֶׁנִּקְבַּע בְּשׁוּשָׁן לְהַשְׁמִיד אוֹתָם, לְהַרְאוֹת לְאֶסְתֵּר וּלְסַפֵּר לָהּ, וּלְצַוּוֹת עָלֶיהָ לָבוֹא אֶל הַמֶּלֶךְ לְהִתְחַנֵּן אֵלָיו וּלְבַקֵּשׁ מִמֶּנּוּ עַל עַמָּהּ.
verses.english: And he also handed him the supplementary proclamation to the sealed written edict that had been delivered to Shushan – whose true intent was to annihilate the Jews – to show to Esther and explain the situation to her.He requested that Hatach instruct Esther to go to the king and beg for his favour, and to plead before him on behalf of her nation.

verses.hebrew: הֲתָךְ בָּא וְסִפֵּר לְאֶסְתֵּר אֶת דִּבְרֵי מָרְדֳּכָי.
verses.english: Armed with this information, Hatach came back to the palace and delivered Mordechai’s message to Esther.

verses.hebrew: אָמְרָה אֶסְתֵּר לַהֲתָךְ וְצִוְּתָה אוֹתוֹ לוֹמַר לְמָרְדֳּכָי:
verses.english: Esther relayed the following reply to Hatach, and instructed him to indirectly forward it to Mordechai. He dared not speak to Mordechai in person for a second time, lest Haman’s men suspect that Mordechai is in cahoots with the queen.

verses.hebrew: כָּל עַבְדֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ וְעַמֵּי מְדִינוֹת הַמֶּלֶךְ יוֹדְעִים שֶׁכָּל אִישׁ אוֹ אִשָּׁה שֶׁיָּבוֹאוּ אֶל הַמֶּלֶךְ אֶל הֶחָצֵר הַפְּנִימִית בְּלִי שֶׁהֻזְמַן דִּינוֹ אֶחָד – לְהֵהָרֵג, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הַמֶּלֶךְ יוֹשִׁיט לוֹ אֶת שַׁרְבִיט הַזָּהָב וְהוּא יִחְיֶה, וַאֲנִי לֹא הֻזְמַנְתִּי לָבוֹא אֶל הַמֶּלֶךְ כְּבָר שְׁלוֹשִׁים יוֹם.
verses.english: “I do not think it is sensible for me to force entry into the king’s court at this time.Firstly, all the king’s courtiers and all the civilians in the king’s provinces know that if any man or woman – and that includes me – enters the king’s presence in the inner court without a summons, there is but one directive for him – there are no exceptional extenuating circumstances. He will be put to death! That is, unless the king extends the golden sceptre to him, in which case he may live.Moreover, I have not been summoned to visit the king for the last thirty days, and it is likely that he will anyway summon me in the near future!I therefore believe it is far more sensible to wait a while and gain a secure audience. For, if I force entry, even if the king pardons me, I will have spent his favour before I even get to commence pleading the case of the Jews.”

verses.hebrew: סִפְּרוּ לְמָרְדֳּכָי אֵת דִּבְרֵי אֶסְתֵּר.
verses.english: And the middlemen relayed Esther’s words to Mordechai.

verses.hebrew: מָרְדֳּכַי אָמַר שֶׁיַּעֲנוּ לְאֶסְתֵּר: אַל תַּחְשְׁבִי לְעַצְמֵךְ לְהִמָּלֵט בְּבֵית הַמֶּלֶךְ וּלְהִנָּצֵל מִמַּה שֶׁיִּקְרֶה לְכָל הַיְּהוּדִים.
verses.english: But Mordechai was concerned that Esther’s apparently conscientious arguments veiled a degree of complacency, and so he instructed them to reply to Esther as follows: “Do not let yourself fantasize that your life is untouchable because of the king’s love for you; that you will escape the fate of the Jews in the king’s palace.”

verses.hebrew: כִּי אִם תִּשְׁתְּקִי עַכְשָׁיו וְלֹא תְּבַקְּשִׁי עֲבוּר הַיְּהוּדִים, תַּגִּיעַ רְוָחָה וְהַצָּלָה לַיְּהוּדִים מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר וְאַתְּ וּמִשְׁפַּחְתֵּךְ תֻּשְׁמְדוּ, וּמִי יוֹדֵעַ אִם לֹא בִּשְׁבִיל הִזְדַּמְּנוּת זוֹ הִגַּעַתְּ לַמַּלְכוּת.
verses.english: “Because if you remain passively silent at this time, I have no doubt that reprieve and salvation will arise for the Jews from someplace else, but if that happens, you and your family heritage will certainly be ‘neutralized’. And, I disagree with your argument that it is more sensible to wait for the king’s summons, because time is of the essence to beat Haman to the king’s ear – who knows, perhaps it is for this very moment that you miraculously entered the monarchy!Esther, your ability to escape punishment and charm the royal court despite your disrespectful and secretive conduct is clearly providential. It suggests that you have merited ongoing Divine protection because the fate of your people rests with you. Should you fail to represent your people for even one moment, I fear the probable course of nature will come back with vengeance, and you will be harshly punished.”

verses.hebrew: אָמְרָה אֶסְתֵּר לַעֲנוֹת לְמָרְדֳּכָי:
verses.english: Esther, upon appreciating that her life was hanging by a thread regardless of her proposed inaction, and emboldened by Mordechai’s faith that even should her petition fail, the Jews will be saved through other means, instructed that the following reply be sent to Mordechai:

verses.hebrew: לֵךְ תְּכַנֵּס אֶת כָּל הַיְּהוּדִים שֶׁנִּמְצְאִים בְּשׁוּשָׁן וְתָצוּמוּ עָלַי, אַל תֹּאכְלוּ וְאַל תִּשְׁתּוּ שְׁלוֹשָׁה יָמִים בַּלַּיְלָה וּבַיּוֹם, גַּם אֲנִי וְהַמְּשָׁרְתוֹת שֶׁלִּי נָצוּם כָּךְ, וְכָךְ אָבוֹא לַמֶּלֶךְ שֶׁלֹּא כָּחוֹק, וְאִם אָמוּת - אָמוּת.
verses.english: “Go, assemble all the Jews present in Shushan, and fast on my behalf. Do not eat or drink for three days, night or day. I and my chambermaids will similarly fast. And then, I shall go to the king against the law, and even if I am to be ‘neutralized’, at least only I shall be ‘neutralized’, whereas the Jews will find other means of salvation!”

verses.hebrew: מָרְדֳּכָי עָבַר בְּשׁוּשָׁן וְעָשָׂה אֶת כָּל מַה שֶּׁצִּוְּתָה עָלָיו אֶסְתֵּר.
verses.english: And Mordechai passed through the Jewish quarter, and proclaimed the fast in accordance with all of Esther’s instructions to him.

verses.hebrew: בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁי לָבְשָׁה אֶסְתֵּר בִּגְדֵי מַלְכוּת וְעָמְדָה בֶּחָצֵר הַפְּנִימִית שֶׁל בֵּית הַמֶּלֶךְ מוּל הֵיכַל הַמֶּלֶךְ, וְהַמֶּלֶךְ יָשַׁב עַל כִּסֵּא מַלְכוּתוֹ בְּהֵיכַל הַמַּלְכוּת מוּל פֶּתַח הַהֵיכָל.
verses.english: On the third day of her fasting, Esther dressed herself in royalty; she looked the epitome of majesty. She went and stood in the king’s inner courtyard opposite the door to the king’s quarters. This maximized her chances of being spotted by the king and presented with the golden sceptre. How providential that the king was sitting at that very moment on his royal throne in his royal quarters, and that it was positioned precisely opposite the door. Normally, the throne was positioned in the courtyard when on public duty, and in the hidden recesses of his private quarters when enjoying time off-duty.

verses.hebrew: כְּשֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ רָאָה אֶת אֶסְתֵּר הַמַּלְכָּה עוֹמֶדֶת בֶּחָצֵר הִיא מָצְאָה חֵן בְּעֵינָיו, הַמֶּלֶךְ הוֹשִׁיט לְאֶסְתֵּר אֶת שַׁרְבִיט הַזָּהָב שֶׁבְּיָדוֹ, אֶסְתֵּר הִתְקָרְבָה וְנָגְעָה בִּקְצֵה הַשַּׁרְבִיט.
verses.english: Now, when the king saw Esther the Queen humbly waiting in the courtyard, even though she was his beloved queen who, in his opinion, was entitled to barge unannounced into his quarters, she found even more favour in his eyes. So, the king extended the golden sceptre to Esther, that providentially he had at hand even though he was off duty. Then Esther approached the king and touched the tip of the sceptre.

verses.hebrew: אָמַר לָהּ הַמֶּלֶךְ: מַה לָּךְ אֶסְתֵּר הַמַּלְכָּה, וּמַה בַּקָּשָׁתֵךְ? גַּם אִם תְּבַקְּשִׁי אֶת חֲצִי הַמַּמְלָכָה זֶה יִנָּתֵן לָךְ!
verses.english: Realizing that if Esther had voluntarily risked her life to see him, something serious must be up, the king said to her, “What threat personally concerns you, Queen Esther? Or, what critical request do you have?”I don’t promise to fulfil your request if it concerns other people, but I am willing to give up half the empire to look after you”.

verses.hebrew: אָמְרָה אֶסְתֵּר: אִם הַמֶּלֶךְ מַסְכִּים, יָבוֹאוּ הַמֶּלֶךְ וְהָמָן הַיּוֹם לִמְסִבַּת שְׁתִיַּת הַיַּיִן שֶׁהֵכַנְתִּי לוֹ.
verses.english: But Esther simply replied, “If it is convenient for the king, I request that the king and Haman come today to the feast that I have already prepared for him”.By inviting Haman to their intimate party, she hoped to demonstrate to Ahasuerus that she had nothing personal against Haman. She simply had to spare her own life along with the lives of those dearest to her – her people. She also hoped to catch Haman off-guard without his advisory team to support him, while the king was inebriated and short-tempered.

verses.hebrew: אָמַר הַמֶּלֶךְ, מַהֲרוּ לִקְרוֹא לְהָמָן כְּדֵי לַעֲשׂוֹת אֶת דִּבְרֵי אֶסְתֵּר, הַמֶּלֶךְ וְהָמָן בָּאוּ לִמְסִבַּת שְׁתִיַּת הַיַּיִן שֶׁאֶסְתֵּר הֵכִינָה.
verses.english: Intrigued, the king accepted the invitation and commanded, “Tell Haman to hurry and do Esther’s bidding – this is Esther’s royal order and he has no choice but to obey”. And thus the king and Haman arrived at the feast that Esther had prepared.

verses.hebrew: אָמַר הַמֶּלֶךְ לְאֶסְתֵּר בִּמְסִבַּת שְׁתִיַּת הַיַּיִן: מַה רְצוֹנֵךְ? הוּא יִנָּתֵן לָךְ! מַה שֶּׁתְּבַקְּשִׁי גַּם עַד חֲצִי הַמַּמְלָכָה יִתְבַּצֵּעַ!
verses.english: At the wine feast, the king asked Esther once again, “What is it that you request for yourself? I have already told you that it shall be granted to you! Or, what critical request do you have on behalf of someone else? I hereby add to my original offer – even if it pertains to no more than half the empire, it shall be fulfilled!”

verses.hebrew: עָנְתָה אֶסְתֵּר וְאָמְרָה, זֹאת בַּקָּשָׁתִי:
verses.english: Esther reflected on this carefully, and responded: “I hesitate to advance my petition, because I only wish to share my personal request and my critical request that relates to others…

verses.hebrew: אִם מָצָאתִי חֵן בְּעֵינֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ וְאִם הַמֶּלֶךְ מַסְכִּים לָתֵת לִי אֶת בַּקָּשָׁתִי, יָבוֹאוּ הַמֶּלֶךְ וְהָמָן לִמְסִבַּת שְׁתִיַּת הַיַּיִן שֶׁאֶעֱשֶׂה לָהֶם, וְאֶעֱשֶׂה אוֹתוֹ מָחָר אִם הַמֶּלֶךְ יַסְכִּים.
verses.english: … if I as a person find favor in the king’s eyes, and if the king assumes it a good idea to grant me this personal request and implement my critical request on behalf of others.Since I only want what is best for the king, and I do not know how much he cherishes me, and I cannot predict how he will take to my request, I dare not share it.But I decided to make it known to the king that there is something big on my mind, and “if indeed I as a person find favor in the king’s eyes, and if indeed the king assumes it will be a good idea to grant me this personal request and implement my critical request on behalf of others”, then the king and Haman shall come to another feast that I shall prepare for them, and tomorrow – should the king instruct me to share what is on my mind – I will be obedient and submit to his command.

verses.hebrew: הָמָן יָצָא בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא שָׂמֵחַ וְטוֹב לֵב, וּכְשֶׁהָמָן רָאָה אֶת מָרְדֳּכַי בְּשַׁעַר הַמֶּלֶךְ שֶׁאֵינוֹ קָם וְלֹא רוֹעֵד מִמֶּנּוּ, הָמָן הִתְמַלֵּא בְּכַעַס עַל מָרְדֳּכַי.
verses.english: That day, the power-hungry Haman left the king’s palace happy and lighthearted. He had finally achieved the status that he so coveted – he was on par with the royals!But as soon as Haman saw Mordechai at the royal gates, who would neither rise nor stir before him, he became filled with inward grievance at Mordechai once more.Haman thought to himself: “Even if he will not bow before me for religious reasons, how dare he not flinch? Does he not realize that I can have him killed for disobedience? He clearly underestimates me! He thinks that I am a powerless nobody!”

verses.hebrew: הָמָן הִתְאַפֵּק שֶׁלֹּא לְהִתְפָּרֵץ וּבָא לְבֵיתוֹ, וְשָׁלַח שֶׁיִּקְרְאוּ לַחֲבֵרָיו וּלְזֶרֶשׁ אִשְׁתּוֹ.
verses.english: Haman repressed his urge to immediately report Mordechai’s misdemeanours to the king, and instead went home, whereupon he sent for his admirers and Zeresh his wife.

verses.hebrew: הָמָן סִפֵּר לָהֶם עַל כְּבוֹדוֹ וְעָשְׁרוֹ וּבָנָיו הָרַבִּים וְכָל מַה שֶּׁהַמֶּלֶךְ רוֹמֵם אוֹתוֹ וְשֶׁקָּבַע אֶת דַּרְגָּתוֹ מֵעַל הַשָּׂרִים וְעַבְדֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ.
verses.english: Haman presented the assembled council with his dilemma. He told them about his staggering successes: His great wealth, his many sons, and all that the king had done to promote him and advance him above all the other officials and courtiers.

verses.hebrew: אָמַר הָמָן: אֲפִלּוּ אֶסְתֵּר הַמַּלְכָּה לֹא הִזְמִינָה עִם הַמֶּלֶךְ אֶל מְסִבַּת שְׁתִיַּת הַיַּיִן שֶׁהֵכִינָה אֶלָּא אוֹתִי, וַאֲנִי מֻזְמָן אֵלֶיהָ עִם הַמֶּלֶךְ גַּם מָחָר.
verses.english: “Moreover”, said Haman, “Queen Esther did not invite anyone besides the king and myself to the feast that she made. And tomorrow too I am invited by her along with the king.She has this big request to make of the king, and so she invited me to back her up and influence the king in her favor! Evidently, I am the most influential man in the empire!”

verses.hebrew: וְכָל זֶה לֹא שָׁוֶה לִי כְּלוּם כָּל זְמָן שֶׁאֲנִי רוֹאֶה אֶת מָרְדֳּכַי הַיְּהוּדִי יוֹשֵׁב בְּשַׁעַר הַמֶּלֶךְ.
verses.english: “Yet, all this grandeur is worthless to me each time I see Mordechai the Jew sitting at the royal gate. As much as I would love to punish him, due to my very greatness, it is beneath my dignity to take his disrespectfulness to heart.”

verses.hebrew: אָמְרוּ לוֹ זֶרֶשׁ אִשְׁתּוֹ וְכָל חֲבֵרָיו: שֶׁיַּעֲשׂוּ עַמּוּד תְּלִיָּה בְּגוֹבַהּ חֲמִשִּׁים אַמָּה (כְּ25 מֶטֶר), וּבַבּוֹקֶר תֹּאמַר לַמֶּלֶךְ וְיִתְלוּ עָלָיו אֶת מָרְדֳּכַי, וְאָז תָּבוֹא עִם הַמֶּלֶךְ אֶל מְסִבַּת שְׁתִיַּת הַיַּיִן שָׂמֵחַ, הַדָּבָר מָצָא חֵן בְּעֵינֵי הָמָן וְהוּא עָשָׂה אֶת עַמּוּד הַתְּלִיָּה.
verses.english: His wife Zeresh and all his admirers expressed the following advice to him, “Let them make use of the stake that is fifty cubits high.”On this stake, lower-class petty criminals were executed without trial and their corpses publicly displayed, to strike terror into the hearts of the populace.“Then, early in the morning, when the fresh corpses are displayed to greet people on their way to work, ask the king to hang Mordechai on it – precisely because he is a lower-class petty criminal. By executing him in this manner, you will emphasize that the nature of his crime was of little consequence. Thus, you can exact vengeance from Mordechai while maintaining a guise of indifference.And then you can accompany the king to the feast happily.”The proposal seemed good in the eyes of Haman, and he made the stake.

verses.hebrew: בַּלַּיְלָה הַהוּא הַמֶּלֶךְ לֹא הִצְלִיחַ לְהֵרָדֵם, הוּא אָמַר שֶׁיָּבִיאוּ אֶת יוֹמַן הַזִּכְרוֹנוֹת וְקָרְאוּ מִמֶּנּוּ לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ.
verses.english: That night, sleep evaded the king. He was intrigued by Esther’s request. “What could she want? She claimed that she had his best interests in mind? Last time she looked out for him, it was to foil the plot of Bigtan and Teresh?!” To attempt to second-guess her, he called for his personal diary, and had the entries read out before him.How providential that he opted for his personal diary rather than the state chronicles, since those had likely been revised by Haman to give himself the credit at Mordechai’s expense.

verses.hebrew: וּמָצְאוּ כָּתוּב שֶׁמָרְדֳּכַי סִפֵּר עַל בִּגְתָנָא וָתֶרֶשׁ שְׁנֵי מְשָׁרְתֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ מִשּׁוֹמְרֵי הַפֶּתַח, שֶׁרָצוּ לְהִתְנַקֵּשׁ בַּמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ.
verses.english: And Ahasuerus found something that caught his eye; that it was Mordechai who had informed on Bigtan and Teresh – two of the king’s valets tasked with guarding the threshold to his quarters – who had plotted to attack King Ahasuerus.The king had totally forgotten about Mordechai’s role, and assumed that his confidantes and especially Haman had been involved in foiling the plot.

verses.hebrew: אָמַר הַמֶּלֶךְ: אֵיזֶה כָּבוֹד וּגְדוּלָּה עָשׂוּ לְמָרְדֳּכַי עַל זֶה? אָמְרוּ נַעֲרֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ מְשָׁרְתָיו: לֹא עָשׂוּ לוֹ שׁוּם דָּבָר.
verses.english: And so the king said, “Which lavish reward shall we bestow on Mordechai, and which promotion shall we offer him – on account of this deed? He is already a courtier on Esther’s account, but his loyalty deserves more public attention.” But the king’s young menservants dismissively replied: “Let us offer him nothing at all.”

verses.hebrew: אָמַר הַמֶּלֶךְ: מִי בֶחָצֵר? וְהָמָן בָּא לֶחָצֵר הַחִיצוֹנָה שֶׁל בֵּית הַמֶּלֶךְ לוֹמַר לַמֶּלֶךְ לִתְלוֹת אֶת מָרְדֳּכַי עַל עַמּוּד הַתְּלִיָּה שֶׁהֵכִין לוֹ.
verses.english: Just then, the king was informed that there was a visitor in his outer courtyard. The king asked, “Who is in the courtyard?”How providential and ironic that precisely at that moment Haman came to the king’s outer courtyard to advise the king to hang Mordechai as an inconsequential petty criminal, on the stake that he had prepared for him.

verses.hebrew: אָמְרוּ נַעֲרֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ אֵלָיו: הִנֵּה הָמָן עוֹמֵד בֶּחָצֵר, אָמַר הַמֶּלֶךְ: יָבוֹא!
verses.english: The king’s young menservants answered him, “It is Haman standing in the court.”“Let him enter,” said the king.

verses.hebrew: הָמָן בָּא, אָמַר לוֹ הַמֶּלֶךְ: מַה לַּעֲשׂוֹת לָאִישׁ שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ רוֹצֶה שֶׁיְּכַבְּדוּ אוֹתוֹ? הָמָן אָמַר לְעַצְמוֹ, לְמִי הַמֶּלֶךְ רוֹצֶה לָתֵת כָּבוֹד יוֹתֵר מִלִּי?!
verses.english: And Haman entered, whereupon the king said to him, “What should be done for a man whom the king desires to lavishly reward?” The king deliberately omitted “and promote”, so that Haman would assume he is the likely lucky recipient, and thus his answer would be neither defensive nor envious.And, as the king had surmised, Haman said to himself, “Whom could the king desire to honour more than me?”

verses.hebrew: אָמַר הָמָן לַמֶּלֶךְ: אִישׁ שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ רוֹצֶה שֶׁיְּכַבְּדוּ אוֹתוֹ –
verses.english: After pondering over it, Haman replied to the king with fake humility: “The greatest reward is the knowledge that one is a person whom the king wishes to honour.”

verses.hebrew: יָבִיאוּ בִּגְדֵי מַלְכוּת שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ לָבַשׁ, וְסוּס שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ רָכַב עָלָיו וְשֶׁשָּׂמוּ כֶּתֶר מַלְכוּת בְּרֹאשׁוֹ.
verses.english: That said, in order to publicize the king’s admiration, let the courtiers bring royal dress that the king himself wore, and a horse on which the king himself rode on his coronation day – upon which the royal crown was set on his head.

verses.hebrew: וְיִמְסְרוּ אֶת הַבְּגָדִים וְאֶת הַסּוּס, לִידֵי אֶחָד מִשָּׂרֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ הַשַּׁלִּיטִים, וְיַלְבִּישׁוּ אֶת הָאִישׁ שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ רוֹצֶה שֶׁיְּכַבְּדוּ אוֹתוֹ, וְיַרְכִּיבוּ אוֹתוֹ עַל הַסּוּס בְּכִכַּר הָעִיר, וְיַכְרִיזוּ לְפָנָיו: כָּכָה עוֹשִׂים לָאִישׁ שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ רוֹצֶה שֶׁיְּכַבְּדוּ אוֹתוֹ!
verses.english: Then, place the royal dress and the horse in the charge of one of the king’s most noble courtiers. Then, have the courtiers attire the man whom the king desires to lavishly reward, and parade him on the horse through the city square and proclaim before him: “Such is done for the man whom the king desires to lavishly reward!”

verses.hebrew: אָמַר הַמֶּלֶךְ לְהָמָן: תְּמַהֵר, קַח אֶת הַבְּגָדִים וְאֶת הַסּוּס כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְתָּ, וְכָךְ תַּעֲשֶׂה לְמָרְדֳּכַי הַיְּהוּדִי שֶׁיּוֹשֵׁב בְּשַׁעַר הַמֶּלֶךְ, אַל תַּחְסִיר שׁוּם דָּבָר מִכָּל מַה שֶּׁאָמַרְתָּ!
verses.english: The king was deeply concerned by Haman’s megalomaniac fantasy to blur the boundaries between himself and the king; “Haman must be put in his place; it is time to divest some of his powers to trustworthy Mordechai who had proved his fidelity to the king.”And so the king said to Haman, “Hurry, I order you to personally take the royal dress and the horse exactly as you said, and I insist that you personally perform this entire ceremony – from the dressing through the parading – for Mordechai the Jew who sits at the royal gate. Do not omit a single detail from what you just described to me!”

verses.hebrew: הָמָן לָקַח אֶת הַבְּגָדִים וְאֶת הַסּוּס, וְהִלְבִּישׁ אֶת מָרְדֳּכָי, וְהִרְכִּיב אוֹתוֹ עַל הַסּוּס בְּכִכַּר הָעִיר, וְקָרָא לְפָנָיו: כָּכָה עוֹשִׂים לָאִישׁ שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ רוֹצֶה שֶׁיְּכַבְּדוּ אוֹתוֹ!
verses.english: So Haman took the royal dress and the horse. He personally dressed Mordechai and paraded him through the city square. He personally proclaimed before him: “Such is done for the man whom the king desires to lavishly reward!”

verses.hebrew: מָרְדֳּכַי חָזַר לְשַׁעַר הַמֶּלֶךְ, וְהָמָן מִהֵר בִּדְחִיפוּת לְבֵיתוֹ, אָבֵל וּמְכַסֶּה אֶת רֹאשׁוֹ בְּבוּשָׁה.
verses.english: How providential that this episode achieved precisely the opposite of what Haman had in mind. Ultimately, Mordechai returned unharmed to the royal gate, while Haman was sent home, mournfully, hanging his head in shame.

verses.hebrew: הָמָן סִפֵּר לְזֶרֶשׁ אִשְׁתּוֹ וּלְכָל חֲבֵרָיו אֶת כָּל מַה שֶּׁקָּרָה לוֹ, אָמְרוּ לוֹ חֲבֵרָיו הַחֲכָמִים וְזֶרֶשׁ אִשְׁתּוֹ: אִם מָרְדֳּכַי שֶׁהִתְחַלְתָּ לִפּוֹל בְּפָנָיו הוּא מִצֶּאֱצָאֵי הַיְּהוּדִים, לֹא תּוּכַל לְנַצֵּחַ אוֹתוֹ אֶלָּא תִּפּוֹל בְּפָנָיו.
verses.english: Haman related the unlucky fate that had befallen him to his wife Zeresh and all his admirers. He hoped they would allay his fear that Mordechai had now become invulnerable. He hoped they would agree that this was an insignificant stroke of bad luck. But, to his dismay, his sage counsellors and even his wife Zeresh replied: “If Mordechai, before whom you have fallen by your own initiative and doing, is a scion of the Jews – the people of providence, you’d best leave him alone. You will not overcome him; you will plummet long before he does.”

verses.hebrew: בְּעוֹד הֵם מְדַבְּרִים אִתּוֹ הִגִּיעוּ מְשָׁרְתֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ וּמִהֲרוּ לְהָבִיא אֶת הָמָן לִמְסִבַּת שְׁתִיַּת הַיַּיִן שֶׁהֵכִינָה אֶסְתֵּר.
verses.english: How providential that while they were still speaking with him, the king’s valets arrived and overheard Haman’s ongoing megalomaniac ambitions that included deposing Mordechai. They harried Haman, for they had orders to quickly bring him to the banquet that Esther had prepared.

verses.hebrew: הַמֶּלֶךְ וְהָמָן בָּאוּ לִשְׁתּוֹת עִם אֶסְתֵּר הַמַּלְכָּה.
verses.english: Esther’s strategy had been right on the mark. The king, following his sleepless night of intrigue, decided to trust Esther. He would order her to share her request, and he was certain that he could grant it. And so, on the back of an eventful 24-hours for both the king and Haman, they arrived at the feast that Esther had made.

verses.hebrew: הַמֶּלֶךְ אָמַר לְאֶסְתֵּר גַּם בַּיּוֹם הַשֵּׁנִי בִּמְסִבַּת שְׁתִיַּת הַיַּיִן: מָה רְצוֹנֵךְ אֶסְתֵּר הַמַּלְכָּה, זֶה יִנָּתֵן לָךְ! וּמַה בַּקָּשָׁתֵךְ, גַּם עַד חֲצִי הַמַּמְלָכָה זֶה יִתְבַּצֵּעַ!
verses.english: As she had hoped, the king again said to Esther, at the wine feast on this second day: “What is your personal request – o Esther the queen whom I love dearly and whose concerns I obviously wish to address – and it shall be granted to you, and what is your critical request on behalf of others – that shall be fulfilled even if it pertains to up to half the empire!

verses.hebrew: עָנְתָה אֶסְתֵּר הַמַּלְכָּה וְאָמְרָה: אִם מָצָאתִי חֵן בְּעֵינֶיךָ הַמֶּלֶךְ וְאִם כָּךְ רְצוֹן הַמֶּלֶךְ, יִנָּתְנוּ לִי לְבַקָּשָׁתִי הַחַיִּים שֶׁלִּי וְשֶׁל עַמִּי!
verses.english: And now Esther the queen responded and said, “If I find favor in your eyes – o King whom I esteem and for whom I only request the best – and if it seems good in the king’s eyes: Let my very life be granted to me for my personal request, and the very lives of my people for my critical other-focused request.

verses.hebrew: כִּי נִמְכַּרְנוּ אֲנִי וְעַמִּי לְהַשְׁמִיד לַהֲרוֹג וּלְאַבֵּד אוֹתָנוּ, אִלּוּ הָיִינוּ נִמְכָּרִים לַעֲבָדִים וְלִשְׁפָחוֹת הָיִיתִי שׁוֹתֶקֶת כִּי עֲדִיפָה צָרָה כָּזוֹ כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה נֶזֶק לַמֶּלֶךְ.
verses.english: For none less than I, as well as my people, have been sold to a treacherous tyrant, to be annihilated, murdered, and “neutralized”. My majesty, you were misled: The tyrant wants blood, not just religious-cultural reformation. And the supposedly insignificant people in his crosshairs are none other than the virtuous Jews. Moreover, I fear that this heinous genocide is all my fault; that the tyrant’s entire scheme is just a pretext to depose me. Had we just been sold to become slaves and maids I would have remained silent, so as not to trouble the king. But, as we have been sold for annihilation, it is this tyrant who is not worth the trouble he causes the king, rather than the people about whom he slanderously claimed, ‘it is not worth the king’s while to let them be’.”

verses.hebrew: אָמַר הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ לְאֶסְתֵּר הַמַּלְכָּה: מִי הוּא זֶה וְאֵיפֹה הוּא הָאִישׁ שֶׁהֶעֱלָה עַל דַּעְתּוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת כָּךְ?!
verses.english: Upon hearing this, King Ahasuerus turned to his aides, and upon their shocked silence, turned to Esther the queen, “Who is the person with such a despicable scheme? And what is the underlying motivation, that the person convinced themselves of the feasibility of such unfathomable action?”

verses.hebrew: אָמְרָה אֶסְתֵּר: אִישׁ עוֹשֶׂה צָרוֹת וְאוֹיֵב – הָמָן הָרָע הַזֶּה! וְהָמָן נִבְהַל וּפָחַד מֵהַמֶּלֶךְ וְהַמַּלְכָּה.
verses.english: Whereupon Esther said, “Indeed, ‘a tyrannical and hateful man’ perfectly describes this evil Haman. He is a person with despicable character – he is a dishonest, cruel and narcissistic megalomaniac, who develops profound and deep-seated hatred towards anyone who crosses his path.”Haman was panic stricken as he was faced by both the king and the queen. He had been exposed, and whatever he could muster in his defense would only make matters worse. To justify his hatred of the Jews would further provoke the queen, and to double down on his plot would confirm that he had lied to the king!

verses.hebrew: וְהַמֶּלֶךְ קָם בְּכַעֲסוֹ מִמְּסִבַּת שְׁתִיַּת הַיַּיִן וְהָלַךְ אֶל גִּנַּת הָאַרְמוֹן, וְהָמָן עָמַד לְבַקֵּשׁ עַל חַיָּיו מֵאֶסְתֵּר הַמַּלְכָּה כִּי הוּא רָאָה שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ כְּבָר הֶחְלִיט לַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ רַע.
verses.english: The king, overwhelmed by his internal aggrievment that he had been tricked by his closest advisor and was now stuck in a bureaucratic nightmare with the life of his queen on the line, arose from the wine feast and headed for the palace garden. Haman remained to plead for his life from Esther the queen, because he saw that, from the king’s perspective, his nasty fate was sealed.

verses.hebrew: וְהַמֶּלֶךְ חָזַר מִגִּנַּת הָאַרְמוֹן לְהֵיכַל שְׁתִיַּת הַיַּיִן, וְהָמָן נוֹפֵל עַל הַמִּטָּה שֶׁאֶסְתֵּר עָלֶיהָ, אָמַר הַמֶּלֶךְ: גַּם לֶאֱנוֹס אֶת הַמַּלְכָּה אֶצְלִי בַּבַּיִת?! הַמִּילִים יָצְאוּ מִפִּי הַמֶּלֶךְ וְהַמְּשָׁרְתִים כִּסּוּ אֶת פְּנֵי הָמָן.
verses.english: When the king returned from the palace garden to the chamber in which the wine feast was held, to his horror he found that Haman had collapsed on the couch on which Esther was reclined. Presuming that Esther had correctly surmised that Haman wished to depose her, he interpreted Haman’s behaviour as a last-ditch attempt to murder her. And so the king furiously declared, “He even attempts to overthrow the queen in my very presence in the palace!”As soon as these words left the king’s mouth, they covered Haman’s face in accordance with Persian tradition that when the king is angry with you, make sure not to be seen.

verses.hebrew: חַרְבוֹנָה, אֶחָד הַמְּשָׁרְתִים שֶׁלִּפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ, אָמַר: גַּם הִנֵּה עַמּוּד הַתְּלִיָּה שֶׁהָמָן עָשָׂה לִתְלוֹת אֶת מָרְדֳּכָי שֶׁדִּבֵּר דְּבָרִים טוֹבִים בִּשְׁבִיל הַמֶּלֶךְ, עוֹמֵד בְּבֵית הָמָן, בְּגוֹבַהּ חֲמִשִּׁים אַמָּה! אָמַר הַמֶּלֶךְ: תְּלוּ אוֹתוֹ עָלָיו!
verses.english: And then Charvona, one of the king’s valets, who had been sent to escort Haman to the feast and had thus overheard Haman’s plot to assassinate Mordechai, spoke up and said: “There is further incriminating evidence from the stake that Haman has made for Mordechai who spoke-up for the king’s benefit when Bigtan and Teresh plotted to assassinate him. Surely Haman’s animosity towards Mordechai confirms that he was party to this plot? Moreover, even though the king has now publicly paraded Mordechai and instructed his promotion, it is still standing in Haman’s home, and he still intends to use it. He does not care that it would publicly humiliate the king if Mordechai was hanged as a petty criminal!”The king had heard enough and ordered: “Hang him on it instead!”

verses.hebrew: תָּלוּ אֶת הָמָן עַל עַמּוּד הַתְּלִיָּה שֶׁהֵכִין לְמָרְדֳּכָי, וְהַמֶּלֶךְ נִרְגַּע מִכַּעֲסוֹ.
verses.english: And so they hanged Haman on the tree that he had prepared for Mordechai, and the inner aggrievement of the king was calmed.

verses.hebrew: בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ נָתַן לְאֶסְתֵּר הַמַּלְכָּה אֶת בֵּיתוֹ שֶׁל הָמָן אוֹיֵב הַיְּהוּדִים, וּמָרְדֳּכַי נִכְנַס לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ כִּי אֶסְתֵּר סִפְּרָה מִי הוּא עֲבוּרָה.
verses.english: Within the space of one day, all of Haman’s power and prestige was handed over to his primary adversary:That very day King Ahasuerus gave the estate of Haman, the arch persecutor of the Jews, to Queen Esther. Had the king executed him for treason against the king, his property would have belonged to the king. This gesture communicated that Haman was primarily executed for treason against the queen, fuelled by his Jew hatred. And Mordechai was promoted such that he could present himself to the king whenever he pleased, for, in addition to his virtues, Esther had revealed how he was related to her.

verses.hebrew: הַמֶּלֶךְ הֵסִיר אֶת טַבַּעַת הַחוֹתֶמֶת שֶׁלּוֹ שֶׁהֶעֱבִיר מֵהָמָן וּנְתָנָהּ לְמָרְדֳּכָי, אֶסְתֵּר מִנְּתָה אֶת מָרְדֳּכַי לִשְׁלוֹט עַל בֵּית הָמָן.
verses.english: The king removed his signet ring that he had reclaimed from Haman, and gave it to Mordechai. Esther put Mordechai in charge of Haman’s estate.

verses.hebrew: אֶסְתֵּר הִמְשִׁיכָה לְדַבֵּר לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ וְנָפְלָה לִפְנֵי רַגְלָיו, וּבָכְתָה וְהִתְחַנְּנָה לוֹ שֶׁיְּבַטֵּל אֶת רָעַת הָמָן הַצֶּאֱצָא שֶׁל אֲגָג, וְאֶת תָּכְנִיתוֹ שֶׁתִּכְנֵן לַעֲשׂוֹת לַיְּהוּדִים.
verses.english: Despite the king’s magnanimous gestures to protect Esther, he had not indicated any willingness to spare the Jews from their fate. Esther appreciated that Ahasuerus was faced with an acute bureaucratic dilemma – Persian etiquette prohibited backtracking on an established law. And while the dictatorial Ahasuerus had no regard for the legal tradition, he certainly did not want to come across as unethical or uncouth.Worried that he was avoiding her request, Esther continued her plea. She reasoned with the king to influence him intellectually, and she fell at his feet and wept to influence him emotionally.She beseeched him to avert the evil decree of Haman the Agagite and the scheme that he intended for the Jews.She argued that standard etiquette did not apply. Firstly, the edict was issued by Haman and not the king – who had been utterly misled; this could hardly be called backtracking. Secondly, since the scrolls were presently unopened, recalling them would not constitute backtracking on established legislation.

verses.hebrew: הַמֶּלֶךְ הוֹשִׁיט לְאֶסְתֵּר אֶת שַׁרְבִיט הַזָּהָב, וְאֶסְתֵּר קָמָה וְנֶעֶמְדָה לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ.
verses.english: The king extended the golden sceptre to Esther to communicate his willingness to listen further, and so Esther arose and stood before the king.

verses.hebrew: וְאָמְרָה: אִם הַמֶּלֶךְ מַסְכִּים וְאִם אֲנִי מוֹצֵאת חֵן בְּעֵינָיו וְהַמֶּלֶךְ חוֹשֵׁב שֶׁזֶּה נָכוֹן וַאֲנִי טוֹבָה בְּעֵינָיו, יִכְתְּבוּ לְבַטֵּל אֶת הַצַּוִּים שֶׁל הַתָּכְנִית שֶׁל הָמָן בֶּן הַמְּדָתָא הַצֶּאֱצָא שֶׁל אֲגָג שֶׁכָּתַב לְהַשְׁמִיד אֶת הַיְּהוּדִים שֶׁבְּכָל מְדִינוֹת הַמֶּלֶךְ.
verses.english: And this is what she said:“If:a) My petition is emotionally attractive –a. its content appeals to the king;b. I, the petitioner, appeal to the king;b) My plan is strategically sound –a. It seems ethically correct to the king. By dissociating himself with such an evil plot while working within the confines of existing etiquette, news of the king’s ethicality would spread across the empire;b. I am sufficiently valuable in his eyes to ensure that I, the queen, do not become a depressed or insane woman –Then:Let an edict be written that all the scrolls containing the scheme of Haman son of Hammedata the Agagite be returned, those in which he wrote to “neutralize” the Jews throughout all the king’s provinces.”

verses.hebrew: כִּי אֵיךְ אוּכַל לִרְאוֹת אֶת הָרַע שֶׁיִּקְרֶה לְעַמִּי?! וְאֵיךְ אוּכַל לִרְאוֹת אֶת הַשְׁמָדַת מִשְׁפַּחְתִּי?!
verses.english: “And the Jews’ safety cannot be secured by appending a second sealed scroll to be opened on the 13th of Adar that will qualify the intention of the first scroll, for how can I cope with beholding the evil that will likely befall my people in the interim now that news of the first scroll’s contents has leaked and the Jews are already perceived as dead-men walking, and how can I cope with beholding the possible demolition of my entire heritage!? How can I be confident that the masses will appreciate legal subtlety, and correctly reinterpret the first scroll in light of the second?

verses.hebrew: אָמַר הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ לְאֶסְתֵּר הַמַּלְכָּה וּלְמָרְדֳּכַי הַיְּהוּדִי: הִנֵּה, אֶת בֵּיתוֹ שֶׁל הָמָן נָתַתִּי לְאֶסְתֵּר, וְאֶת הָמָן תָּלוּ עַל עַמּוּד הַתְּלִיָּה עַל שֶׁהִתְנַכֵּל לַיְּהוּדִים.
verses.english: The king rejected Esther’s first plan but was willing to pursue her second plan. He believed it would be both ethically viable and sufficiently effective.This is what King Ahasuerus replied to Esther the queen and Mordechai the Jew: Look, I have already handed Haman’s estate to Esther and hanged him on the stake for his attempt to harm the Jews. Does this not broadcast that Haman abused my trust and acted against my Jewish queen? Haven’t my actions already undermined the credibility of the first scroll? Won’t the masses now read the scrolls very carefully to ensure that their behaviour towards the Jews is lawful?

verses.hebrew: וְאַתֶּם כִּתְבוּ עַל הַיְּהוּדִים מַה שֶּׁאַתֶּם רוֹצִים בְּצַו חָדָשׁ בְּשֵׁם הַמֶּלֶךְ וְתַחְתְּמוּ בְּחוֹתֶמֶת טַבַּעַת הַמֶּלֶךְ, כִּי צַו שֶׁנִּכְתָּב בְּשֵׁם הַמֶּלֶךְ וְנֶחְתַּם בְּחוֹתֶמֶת הַמֶּלֶךְ אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְבַטֵּל.
verses.english: I suggest that you write a second scroll to clarify and reinterpret the wording of the first edict, in such a manner that you deem favourable to the Jews.Perhaps transform the Jews from the object to the subject by adding clarification as follows:To destroy, massacre, and neutralize–TO BE IMPLEMENTED BY –all the Jews,–TO BE IMPLEMENTED ON THEIR ENEMY –from the young to the old, children and women.Write this clarification in the name of the king and sign it with the royal signet. Because, in my opinion, even in circumstances such as these, an edict that has been previously written in the king’s name and signed with the king’s signet may not be recalled.

verses.hebrew: סוֹפְרֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ הֻזְמְנוּ אָז – בְּיוֹם כ"ג בַּחוֹדֶשׁ הַשְּׁלִישִׁי הוּא חוֹדֶשׁ סִיוָן, וְכָתְבוּ אֶת כָּל מַה שֶּׁצִּוָּה מָרְדֳּכַי אֶל הַיְּהוּדִים וְאֶל הַנְּצִיבִים וְהַמּוֹשְׁלִים וְשָׂרֵי הַמְּדִינוֹת שֶׁמֵּהוֹדּוּ וְעַד כּוּשׁ מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים וְשֶׁבַע מְדִינוֹת, לְכָל מְדִינָה וּמְדִינָה בִּכְתָבָהּ וּלְכָל עַם וְעַם בִּשְׂפָתוֹ, וְאֶל הַיְּהוּדִים בִּכְתָבָם וּבִשְׂפָתָם.
verses.english: Some time thereafter, in the third month of the Jewish calendar, that is on the twenty-third day of Sivan, the king’s scribes were summoned. Mordechai and Esther decided to wait until the couriers had returned from delivering the first scrolls so that they could use the same couriers to deliver the second scrolls. This would increase the credibility of the second scrolls and prove that they were not forged.The scrolls were written as per Mordechai’s instructions and addressed to the Jews, the king’s satraps and governors, and the officials of every one of the 127 nations from India to North-West Africa. They wrote to every province in its own script and to every people in their own language. They also addressed the Jews in their own script and their own language.The second scrolls were more widely disseminated than the first scrolls issued by Haman. This time, there were additional scrolls uniquely addressed to the Jews, and scrolls sent to local officials across the entire breadth of the empire. Conversely, Haman had sufficed with sending scrolls to the main regional authorities in the more far-flung reaches of the empire. The addition of new addressees who had not received the first scroll would further establish the second scroll’s primacy over the first.

verses.hebrew: הוּא כָּתַב בְּשֵׁם הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ וְחָתַם בְּחוֹתֶמֶת הַמֶּלֶךְ וְשָׁלַח מִכְתָּבִים בְּיַד הַדּוֹהֲרִים עַל הַפְּרָדִים בְּנֵי סוּסוֹת מֵרְכוּשׁ הַמֶּלֶךְ.
verses.english: Mordechai wrote the new edicts in the name of King Ahasuerus and sealed them with the king’s signet. He dispatched them as scrolls with high-speed couriers riding on horseback with the select steeds of the royal stables.

verses.hebrew: וְנִכְתַּב שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ נָתַן רְשׁוּת לַיְּהוּדִים שֶׁבְּכָל עִיר לְהִתְכַּנֵּס וְלַעֲמוֹד בַּקְּרָב כְּדֵי לְהַצִּיל אֶת נַפְשָׁם, וּלְהַשְׁמִיד וְלַהֲרוֹג וּלְאַבֵּד כָּל צָבָא שֶׁל עַם וּמְדִינָה שֶׁנִּלְחָם בָּהֶם, וְאֶת הַיְּלָדִים וְהַנָּשִׁים, וְלָקַחַת אֶת שְׁלָלָם.
verses.english: And this is what they proclaimed: “That the king had granted permission to the Jews in each and every city to congregate and rise-up to fight for their lives. They may destroy, massacre, and “neutralize” any armies of all peoples and provinces that persecute them, along with their women and children.And, they may plunder their possessions –

verses.hebrew: בְּיוֹם אֶחָד בְּכָל מְדִינוֹת הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ, בְּיוֹם י"ג לַחוֹדֶשׁ הַשְּׁנֵים עָשָׂר הוּא חוֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר.
