verses.english: But only on that single day, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, that is, the month of Adar.Whereas Haman’s edict implied that there was no deadline for the plunder – to encourage people to murder as many Jews as possible on the 13th and plunder afterwards – Mordechai’s edict expressly limited the plunder to the 13th as well. The reason for this was that Mordechai thought it distasteful for the Jews to plunder. By limiting the right to plunder to the day when the Jews would be otherwise occupied with killing their enemies, he effectively ensured that they wouldn’t act on this right.Moreover, Mordechai emphasized in each scroll that this edict was disseminated and applied in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus. Hopefully, this would counter Haman’s attempt to conceal the widespread genocidal nature of the edict in the first scroll.In summation, this is what the second scroll looked like, with Mordechai’s qualifications capitalized and italicized:–TO : ALL THE KING’S SATRAPS AND GOVERNORS, AND THE OFFICIALS OF EVERY ONE OF THE 127 NATIONS FROM INDIA TO NORTH-WEST AFRICA –You are hereby instructed:To destroy, massacre, and neutralize–TO BE IMPLEMENTED BY –all the Jews,–TO BE IMPLEMENTED ON THEIR ENEMY –from the young to the old, children and women.–AND TO PLUNDER THEIR POSSESSIONS –on a single day, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month – that is, the month of Adar.

verses.hebrew: תּוֹכֶן הַכְּתָב: יִקָּבַע חוֹק בְּכָל מְדִינָה, וְיִתְפַּרְסֵם אֵצֶל כָּל הָעַמִּים, שֶׁהַיְּהוּדִים יִתְכּוֹנְנוּ לַיּוֹם הַזֶּה לִנְקוֹם בְּאוֹיְבֵיהֶם.
verses.english: He also sent a supplement to the sealed written edicts, that was to be legally enacted in each province and publicised among all the nations. It stated: The Jews shall be militarily prepared for that day – the 13th of Adar – to exact revenge from their enemies. But, once again, the scrolls themselves were not to be opened before the 13th of Adar.

verses.hebrew: הַדּוֹהֲרִים עַל הַפְּרָדִים מֵרְכוּשׁ הַמֶּלֶךְ יָצְאוּ בִּמְהִירוּת וּבִדְחִיפוּת כְּדִבְרֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ וְהַחוֹק נִקְבַּע בְּשׁוּשַׁן הַבִּירָה.
verses.english: The couriers, riding the select steeds of the royal stables, departed in a state of confusion and frenzy at the king’s command; and only once they had left, the law was enacted in the capital Shushan. Like Haman before him, Mordechai wanted to ensure that the edicts were dispatched before local lobbyists could become aware of their contents and petition the king to block them.

verses.hebrew: וּמָרְדֳּכַי יָצָא מִלִּפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ בִּלְבוּשׁ מַלְכוּת שֶׁל תְּכֵלֶת וְלָבָן וּבְכֶתֶר זָהָב גָּדוֹל וְצָעִיף פִּשְׁתָּן וְצָעִיף אַרְגָּמָן, וּבָעִיר שׁוּשָׁן צָהֲלוּ וְשָׂמְחוּ.
verses.english: Only once he secured his people’s future did Mordechai go public with his newfound status. Mordechai then went out from the king’s presence in royal robes of indigo-blue and white cotton, with a large crown of gold and a mantle of fine linen and purple. And the entire wider city of Shushan – Jewish and non-Jewish inhabitants alike – rang with joyous cries and was delighted that megalomanic Haman had been replaced by pious Mordechai.

verses.hebrew: לַיְּהוּדִים הָיָה אוֹר בָּעֵינַיִם וְשִׂמְחָה וְשָׂשׂוֹן וְכָבוֹד.
verses.english: As for the Jews, they enjoyed light and happiness; they rejoiced and were honoured.

verses.hebrew: וּבְכָל מְדִינָה וּבְכָל עִיר כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁדִּבְרֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ וְהַחוֹק שֶׁלּוֹ מִתְפַּרְסְמִים, יֵשׁ שִׂמְחָה וְשָׂשׂוֹן לַיְּהוּדִים, סְעוּדָה עִם יַיִן וְיוֹם טוֹב, וְרַבִּים מִבְּנֵי הָעַמִּים שֶׁבָּאֲרָצוֹת מִתְגַּיְּרִים מֵרוֹב פַּחַד מֵהַיְּהוּדִים.
verses.english: And in every province and in every city – since Mordechai’s scrolls were dispatched to each and every city, to ensure a wider coverage than those of Haman – wherever the king’s command and edict arrived, there was happiness and rejoicing among the Jews, and celebratory feasts and religious holidays were declared. Many of the other peoples of those lands wished they were Jews, for the fear of the Jews fell upon them.Thus, the plan of Ahasuerus succeeded in quelling any interim uprisings against the Jews; Esther’s concerns that the Jews would be subject to abuses even before the 13th of Adar were allayed.

verses.hebrew: וּבַחוֹדֶשׁ הַשְּׁנֵים עָשָׂר הוּא חוֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר בְּיוֹם י"ג בּוֹ, כְּשֶׁהִגִּיעַ זְמַן בִּצּוּעַ הַחוֹק שֶׁל פְּקֻדַּת הַמֶּלֶךְ, בַּיּוֹם שֶׁאוֹיְבֵי הַיְּהוּדִים תִּכְנְנוּ לִשְׁלוֹט בָּהֶם, קָרָה הַהֵיפֶךְ, שֶׁהַיְּהוּדִים הֵם שֶׁשָּׁלְטוּ בְּשׂוֹנְאֵיהֶם.
verses.english: On the thirteenth day of the twelfth month—that is, the month of Adar, the scrolls were opened. The king’s edicts inscribed in them reached the masses and it was time to act upon them.How providential that on the very day that the enemies of the Jews had hoped to overcome them, the opposite happened; the Jews were the ones who overcame their enemies.One of the hallmarks of providence is when a scheme turns on its head; when, not only does it fail to accomplish its aims, but it actually accomplishes the very opposite of its aims. First Haman, and now all the Jew haters met their ends in this very providential fashion.

verses.hebrew: הַיְּהוּדִים הִתְכַּנְּסוּ בְּעָרֵיהֶם בְּכָל מְדִינוֹת הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ כְּדֵי לִפְגּוֹעַ בְּאֵלֶּה שֶׁחִפְּשׂוּ אֶת רָעָתָם, וְאַף אֶחָד לֹא נִסָּה לַעֲמוֹד בִּפְנֵיהֶם כִּי כָּל הָעַמִּים פָּחֲדוּ מֵהֶם.
verses.english: Providentially, the legal mess caused by the two scrolls paralyzed the enemies of the Jews into inaction, and they encountered no organized resistance.The Jews who were clearly entitled by the second scroll to hunt down their persecutors congregated in their cities, throughout the provinces of King Ahasuerus, to attack those who sought to harm them.Conversely, the Jew-haters were confused by the mixed messages: Was the second scroll an addition to the first, or a reinterpretation of the first? Were both the Jew-haters and the Jews permitted to attack one another, or were the Jews alone permitted to attack? Thus, no layman resisted them, for their awe had befallen all the peoples, leading them to err on the side of caution.

verses.hebrew: וְכָל שָׂרֵי הַמְּדִינוֹת וְהַנְּצִיבִים וְהַמּוֹשְׁלִים וְעוֹבְדֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ כִּבְּדוּ אֶת הַיְּהוּדִים כִּי הֵם פָּחֲדוּ מִמָּרְדֳּכַי.
verses.english: Moreover, in all the fortified cities and centres of local government, the officials of the provinces, the satraps, the governors, and members of the king’s civil service, promoted the Jews and their cause. This was not because they particularly loved the Jews, but because fear of Mordechai befell them.Despite their doubts as to the legality of the second scroll which for all intents and purposes revoked an earlier law, Mordechai’s intentions were clear and nobody dared to mess with him.

verses.hebrew: כִּי מָרְדֳּכַי הָיָה חָשׁוּב בְּבֵית הַמֶּלֶךְ וְהַשֵּׁם שֶׁלּוֹ הִתְפַּרְסֵם בְּכָל הַמְּדִינוֹת כִּי הָאִישׁ מָרְדֳּכַי הוֹלֵךְ וּמִתְחַזֵּק.
verses.english: For over the course of the year, Mordechai had become an impressive presence in running the king’s palace, and word of his political acumen spread throughout the provinces. Moreover, Mordechai’s personal status spread continually abroad, upon successfully devising and directing military campaigns.

verses.hebrew: הַיְּהוּדִים הִכּוּ אֶת כָּל אוֹיְבֵיהֶם בְּחֶרֶב וְהָרְגוּ וְהִשְׁמִידוּ אוֹתָם, וְעָשׂוּ בְּשׂוֹנְאֵיהֶם כִּרְצוֹנָם.
verses.english: And so, on the 13th, encountering no military resistance, the Jews subjected their openly declared enemies who had a persecutory track-record to the sword, death and “neutralization”, and behaved towards their covert haters as they pleased.While the edict only sanctioned killing those who had actively persecuted the Jews, the political climate enabled the harassment and subjugation of all Jew-haters.

verses.hebrew: וּבְשׁוּשַׁן הַבִּירָה הָרְגוּ הַיְּהוּדִים וְהִשְׁמִידוּ חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת אִישׁ.
verses.english: In Shushan, the capital city, the Jews killed five hundred men –

verses.hebrew: וְהָרְגוּ אֶת פַּרְשַׁנְדָּתָא וְאֶת דַּלְפוֹן וְאֶת אַסְפָּתָא,
verses.english: Along with: Parshandata, Dalfon, Aspata,

verses.hebrew: וְאֶת פּוֹרָתָא וְאֶת אֲדַלְיָא וְאֶת אֲרִידָתָא,
verses.english: Porata, Adalia, Aridata,

verses.hebrew: וְאֶת פַּרְמַשְׁתָּא וְאֶת אֲרִיסַי וְאֶת אֲרִדַי וְאֶת וַיְזָתָא,
verses.english: Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Vaizata –

verses.hebrew: עֲשֶׂרֶת בְּנֵי הָמָן בֶּן הַמְּדָתָא אוֹיֵב הַיְּהוּדִים, וְהֵם לֹא הוֹשִׁיטוּ יָד לָקַחַת מֵהַשָּׁלָל.
verses.english: the ten sons of Haman son of Hammedata, arch persecutor of the Jews. And in accordance with Mordechai’s implied wishes, they did not lay their hands on the spoils. They acted purely out of self-defence, without lust and greed.

verses.hebrew: בְּאוֹתוֹ יוֹם הוֹדִיעוּ לַמֶּלֶךְ אֶת מִסְפַּר הַהֲרוּגִים בְּשׁוּשַׁן הַבִּירָה.
verses.english: On that day, the vast number of the openly persecutory Jew-haters who had been slain was brought to the king’s attention.

verses.hebrew: אָמַר הַמֶּלֶךְ לְאֶסְתֵּר הַמַּלְכָּה: בְּשׁוּשַׁן הַבִּירָה הַיְּהוּדִים הָרְגוּ וְהִשְׁמִידוּ חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת אִישׁ וְאֶת עֲשֶׂרֶת בְּנֵי הָמָן, בִּשְׁאָר מְדִינוֹת הַמֶּלֶךְ מִי יוֹדֵעַ מֶה עָשׂוּ! וּמָה רְצוֹנֵךְ וְיִנָּתֵן לָךְ וּמַה עוֹד אַתְּ מְבַקֶּשֶׁת וְזֶה יִתְבַּצֵּעַ!
verses.english: The king, shocked at their vast numbers, said to Esther the queen: “If in Shushan the capital – under my very nose – the Jews executed and neutralized five hundred actively persecutory Jew-hating men besides the sons of Haman, how did they fare in my other royal provinces where they likely faced much stiffer resistance? Your position is still vulnerable; Do you have any further personal requests – they shall be granted to you! Do you have any further critical requests on behalf of others – they shall be implemented!

verses.hebrew: אָמְרָה אֶסְתֵּר: אִם הַמֶּלֶךְ מַסְכִּים, יִתְאַפְשֵׁר גַּם מָחָר לַיְּהוּדִים שֶׁבְּשׁוּשָׁן, לַעֲשׂוֹת כְּמוֹ הַחוֹק שֶׁל הַיּוֹם, וְאֶת גּוּפוֹתֵיהֶם שֶׁל עֲשֶׂרֶת בְּנֵי הָמָן יִתְלוּ עַל עַמּוּד הַתְּלִיָּה.
verses.english: Esther wisely requested: “If it seems good to the king, let the Jews in wider Shushan – outside the fortress city – be permitted to act tomorrow as they did today; and let Haman’s ten executed sons be impaled on the stake for all to see.By indicating that your protection of the Jews extends beyond the one-off edict of the 13th of Adar, and by hanging arch Jew-haters such as Haman’s sons on the royal stakes, news of the king’s ongoing support for the Jewish cause will be spread far and wide, and suppress the malice in the hearts of the remaining Jew-haters.”

verses.hebrew: הַמֶּלֶךְ אָמַר שֶׁכָּךְ יֵעָשֶׂה וְנִקְבַּע הַחוֹק בְּשׁוּשָׁן, וְאֶת עֲשֶׂרֶת בְּנֵי הָמָן תָּלוּ.
verses.english: The king agreed with Esther’s strategy and ordered its implementation, and the edict was asserted in Shushan. And so, Haman’s ten sons were hanged.

verses.hebrew: וְהַיְּהוּדִים שֶׁבְּשׁוּשָׁן הִתְכַּנְּסוּ גַּם בְּיוֹם י"ד לְחוֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר, וְהָרְגוּ בְּשׁוּשָׁן שְׁלוֹשׁ מֵאוֹת אִישׁ, וְלֹא הוֹשִׁיטוּ יָד לָקַחַת מֵהַשָּׁלָל.
verses.english: And then the Jews in Shushan gathered again on the 14th day of Adar and killed a further three hundred men in Shushan. Once again, they did not lay their hands on the spoils.

verses.hebrew: וּשְׁאָר הַיְּהוּדִים שֶׁבִּמְדִינוֹת הַמֶּלֶךְ הִתְכַּנְּסוּ וְעָמְדוּ עַל נַפְשָׁם וְהָיָה לָהֶם שֶׁקֶט מֵאוֹיְבֵיהֶם, וְהֵם הָרְגוּ בְּשׂוֹנְאֵיהֶם שִׁבְעִים וַחֲמִשָּׁה אֶלֶף, וְלֹא הוֹשִׁיטוּ יָד לָקַחַת מֵהַשָּׁלָל.
verses.english: Indeed, Ahasuerus’ concerns for the fate of the rest of the Jews throughout the king’s provinces – especially those living outside fortified cities who did not enjoy the protection of the local government and royal garrison stationed there – were not ill-founded. They gathered and fought for their lives against organized militias of Jew-haters until eventually they were relieved of their overt enemies. In the course of fighting, they overstepped the boundaries of the law and killed a further seventy-five thousand of their covert haters – those presumed to possess Amalekite roots. But despite taking this legal liberty, they did not lay hands on the spoils.

verses.hebrew: בְּיוֹם י"ג לְחוֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר הֵם נִלְחֲמוּ, וְהָיָה לָהֶם שֶׁקֶט בְּיוֹם י"ד בּוֹ וְעָשׂוּ אוֹתוֹ יוֹם סְעוּדָה עִם יַיִן וְשִׂמְחָה.
verses.english: The fierce combat, the Jews’ triumph and the Amalek assassinations, all took place on the 13th day of the month of Adar. Then they rested on the 14th of the month, declaring it a day of feasting and celebration.

verses.hebrew: וְהַיְּהוּדִים שֶׁבְּשׁוּשָׁן הִתְכַּנְּסוּ לְהִלָּחֵם בְּיוֹם י"ג בַּחוֹדֶשׁ וְגַם בְּיוֹם י"ד, וְהָיָה לָהֶם שֶׁקֶט בְּיוֹם ט"ו וְעָשׂוּ אוֹתוֹ יוֹם סְעוּדָה עִם יַיִן וְשִׂמְחָה.
verses.english: Conversely, the Jews in Shushan gathered on both the 13th and 14th of the month, and so they only rested on the 15th, declaring it a day of feasting and celebration.

verses.hebrew: לָכֵן הַיְּהוּדִים הַ"פְּרָזִים" – אֵלֶּה שֶׁיּוֹשְׁבִים בְּעָרִים שֶׁאֵינָם מֻקָּפוֹת חוֹמָה, עוֹשִׂים בְּיוֹם י"ד לְחוֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר יוֹם שִׂמְחָה וּסְעוּדָה עִם יַיִן וְיוֹם טוֹב וְשׁוֹלְחִים מָנוֹת אִישׁ לַחֲבֵרוֹ.
verses.english: Given the above fortunate military victory, the diaspora Jews who lived in the unwalled towns experienced the 13th of Adar as a day of salvation – the day on which they were spared from death at the hands of Jew-hating militias. Hence, they began to annually observe the 14th day of the month of Adar as a day of celebration and feasting and a religious holiday, on which they send gifts to one another.Meanwhile, the Jews in the fortified cities were unaware how precarious their situation had been even after the sending of the second scrolls. They did not realize that if not for the fear of Mordechai, a much more deadly interpretation of the scrolls may have been adopted. Thus, from their perspective, nothing particularly noteworthy transpired on the 13th of Adar – the true salvation from their perspective occurred earlier, as soon as Mordechai replaced Haman and sent the second scrolls.

verses.hebrew: מָרְדֳּכַי כָּתַב אֶת הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה, וְשָׁלַח מִכְתָּבִים אֶל כָּל הַיְּהוּדִים שֶׁבְּכָל מְדִינוֹת הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ, הַקְּרוֹבִים וְהָרְחוֹקִים.
verses.english: Because they failed to appreciate the full picture, Mordechai recorded these events and dispatched them as scrolls to all the Jews throughout the provinces of King Ahasuerus, both near and far. It was important to him that all the Jews fully appreciate the true extent of their salvation on the 13th of Adar.

verses.hebrew: שֶׁיְּקַבְּלוּ עַל עַצְמָם לַעֲשׂוֹת אֶת יוֹם י"ד לְחוֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר וְאֶת יוֹם ט"ו בּוֹ בְּכָל שָׁנָה וְשָׁנָה.
verses.english: And he instructed them to adopt the existing practice of the village Jews and observe the 14th and 15th days of Adar each and every year.

verses.hebrew: כְּמוֹ הַיָּמִים שֶׁהָיָה לַיְּהוּדִים שֶׁקֶט מֵאוֹיְבֵיהֶם, וְהַחוֹדֶשׁ שֶׁנֶּהְפַּךְ לָהֶם מִצַּעַר לְשִׂמְחָה וּמֵאֵבֶל לְיוֹם טוֹב, לַעֲשׂוֹת אוֹתָם יָמִים שֶׁל סְעוּדָה עִם יַיִן וְשִׂמְחָה וּשְׁלִיחַת מָנוֹת אִישׁ לַחֲבֵרוֹ וּמַתָּנוֹת לַעֲנִיִּים.
verses.english: On the corresponding days on which they had enjoyed relief from their overt enemies – that is, on the 14th or 15th – during the month that had been transformed for them from one to be associated with grief to one associated with happiness, and from one to be associated with mourning to one associated with religious festivities. He instructed them to express this happiness by instituting these dates as days for feasting, celebration and sending gifts to one another, and to express the religious undertones of this festival by donating charitable presents to the poor.Mordechai taught them that it is against Jewish law to add religious festivals with classical festival flavour to those explicitly mentioned in the Torah. Therefore, they must adopt this new avenue for expressing the religious character of the day.

verses.hebrew: וְהַיְּהוּדִים קִבְּלוּ עַל עַצְמָם אֶת מַה שֶּׁהֵם כְּבָר הִתְחִילוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת וְאֶת מַה שֶׁמָּרְדֳּכַי כָּתַב לָהֶם.
verses.english: And all the Jews accepted upon themselves to abide by what they had already begun to do in the diaspora beyond the fortified cities and to conduct themselves in accordance with the Torah-legal guidance in the writings of Mordechai to them.

verses.hebrew: כִּי הָמָן בֶּן הַמְּדָתָא הַצֶּאֱצָא שֶׁל אֲגָג אוֹיֵב כָּל הַיְּהוּדִים תִּכְנֵן לְהַשְׁמִיד אֶת הַיְּהוּדִים, וְהִגְרִיל גּוֹרָל מָתַי לַעֲשׂוֹת בָּהֶם מְהוּמוֹת וּלְהַשְׁמִיד אוֹתָם.
verses.english: Because Mordechai’s scrolls made unequivocally clear how Haman son of Hammedata the Agagite, was in fact the arch persecutor of all the Jews, and how while he had initially plotted to “neutralize” the religion and culture of the Jews alone, he upon casting the pur – that is, the lot – became increasingly superstitious and determined to crush and exterminate them.

verses.hebrew: וּכְשֶׁאֶסְתֵּר בָּאָה לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ, הַמֶּלֶךְ אָמַר לִכְתּוֹב בַּמִּכְתָּבִים שֶׁהַתָּכְנִית הָרָעָה שֶׁהָמָן חָשַׁב עַל הַיְּהוּדִים תִּתְהַפֵּךְ עָלָיו, וְתָלוּ אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בָּנָיו עַל הָעֵץ.
verses.english: And how even when Esther came before the king to beseech him to recall Haman’s decree, he refused to do so and instead commanded: “The evil plot must be turned on its head without invalidating the first scroll, and that is why they hanged him and his sons on the stake.How scare tactics were necessary precisely because the first scroll had ongoing legal; how the Jew-haters largely ignoring the first edict was very fortunate.

verses.hebrew: לָכֵן קָרְאוּ לַיָּמִים הָאֵלֶּה "פּוּרִים" שֶׁפֵּרוּשׁוֹ גּוֹרָלוֹת, עַל שֵׁם הַגּוֹרָל. לָכֵן נִכְתְּבוּ כָּל דִּבְרֵי הַמְּגִלָּה הַזֹּאת – מָה רָאוּ שֶׁמִּשּׁוּם כָּךְ קָבְעוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת כָּךְ וּמָה קָּרָה לָהֶם –
verses.english: For this reason – namely, the utter reversal of the fortunes of Haman and the Jews – they called these days “Purim” – lots.And because of all the contents of this letter that clarified the providence behind the events they had seen, and the fate that actually befell them –

verses.hebrew: הַיְּהוּדִים קָבְעוּ וְקִבְּלוּ עַל עַצְמָם וְעַל צֶאֱצָאֵיהֶם וְעַל כָּל הַגֵּרִים שֶׁמִּתְלַוִּים אֲלֵיהֶם שֶׁלֹּא יִתְבַּטֵל לְעוֹלָם, שֶׁיַּחְגְּגוּ אֶת שְׁנֵי הַיָּמִים הָאֵלֶּה בִּזְמַנָּם כְּפִי שֶׁנִּכְתְּבוּ, בְּכָל שָׁנָה וְשָׁנָה.
verses.english: They formalized and accepted upon themselves and their descendants, and upon all who join them stipulating that it be an irrevocable religious commitment, to observe these two days, each year, at the proper time – the 14th for unfortified settlements and the 15th for fortified settlements – centred around their writings that shall be publicly read on these days.

verses.hebrew: וְהַיָּמִים הָאֵלֶּה מְצֻיָּנִים וְנֶחְגָּגִים בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר, בְּכָל מִשְׁפָּחָה וּמִשְׁפָּחָה בְּכָל מְדִינָה וּמְדִינָה וּבְכָל עִיר וְעִיר, וִימֵי הַפּוּרִים הָאֵלֶּה לֹא יִתְבַּטְּלוּ מִמִּנְהֲגֵי הַיְּהוּדִים וְצֶאֱצָאֵיהֶם לֹא יַפְסִיקוּ לַחְגּוֹג בָּהֶם.
verses.english: And indeed these days are recalled through reading this scroll and observed through celebration, feasts and gifts, in every generation, in every family, in every diaspora province, and in every fortified city. And due to the stipulation of irrevocability, these days of Purim shall never be removed from the Jews’ calendar, and their memory shall never die out among their descendants.POSTSCRIPT:

verses.hebrew: אֶסְתֵּר הַמַּלְכָּה בַּת אֲבִיחַיִל וּמָרְדֳּכַי הַיְּהוּדִי כָּתְבוּ וְחִיְּבוּ בְּכָל תּוֹקֶף לְקַיֵּם אֶת צַו הָאִגֶּרֶת הַשְּׁנִיָּה – לְקַיֵּם אֶת יְמֵי הַפּוּרִים.
verses.english: But it was not plain sailing – there was one further hurdle to overcome. Religious-legal controversy broke out whether this scroll was worthy of canonization, and whether it was acceptable to tamper with the Sinaitic Torah by formally establishing a new religious holiday.Mordechai and Esther so firmly believed in the value of the scroll and the feasibility of the new holiday, that Queen Esther daughter of Avichayil and Mordechai the Jew used their combined royal and religious authorities and wrote an affidavit confirming the validity of the complete Purim document in its second edition – that added this postscript alluding to the controversy and Mordechai and Esther’s emphatic response.

verses.hebrew: וּמָרְדֳּכַי שָׁלַח מִכְתָּבִים אֶל כָּל הַיְּהוּדִים, אֶל מֵאָה עֶשְׂרִים וְשֶׁבַע הַמְּדִינוֹת שֶׁל מַלְכוּת אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ, וּבָהֶם דִּבְרֵי שָׁלוֹם וּקְבִיעָה,
verses.english: And Mordechai dispatched the second edition of the scrolls to all the Jews in the hundred and twenty-seven provinces of Ahasuerus’s empire, emphasizing that they are words that are both diplomatic and true. They apologized for exercising secular political power, emphasizing that they were compelled to do so to uphold the religious truth and preserve Jewish unity.

verses.hebrew: שֶׁיִּקְבְּעוּ אֶת יְמֵי הַפּוּרִים הָאֵלֶּה בִּזְמַנֵּיהֶם כְּמוֹ שֶׁקָּבְעוּ עֲבוּרָם מָרְדֳּכַי הַיְּהוּדִי וְאֶסְתֵּר הַמַּלְכָּה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁקִּבְּלוּ עַל עַצְמָם וְעַל צֶאֱצָאֵיהֶם, אֶת דִּבְרֵי הַצּוֹמוֹת וְהַזְּעָקָה בָּהֶם.
verses.english: And they explained the crux of their argument: That these days of Purim shall be formally observed at their proper times by man-made commitment, just as Mordechai the Jew and Esther the queen had committed themselves, and just as Jews have committed themselves and their descendants to formally observing the fast days with their lamentations. Their thesis was convincing: It is permissible to add religious holidays and fast-days to the Jewish calendar if they are clearly stipulated as man-made bottom-up customs, and not top-down Divinely-communicated laws.

verses.hebrew: כְּפִי שֶׁאָמְרָה אֶסְתֵּר – הוּא קָבַע דִּבְרֵי הַפּוּרִים הָאֵלֶּה, כַּכָּתוּב בַּמִּכְתָּבִים.
verses.english: And Esther’s thesis was successful; it validated these matters concerning the Purim festival, and had the story included in the written canon.

verses.hebrew: הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ הֵטִיל מַס עַל תּוֹשְׁבֵי הָאָרֶץ וְאִיֵּי הַיָּם, לְאַחַר הַהֲנָחָה בַּמָּס שֶׁבְּהַמְלָכַת אֶסְתֵּר.
verses.english: Assisted by Mordechai’s wise counsel, King Ahasuerus’ influence spread far and wide; he imposed tribute on many regions of the mainland as well as the isles of the seas.

verses.hebrew: וְכָל סִפּוּרֵי הַחוֹזֶק וְהַגְּבוּרָה שֶׁל אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ וּפִרְטֵי גְּדֻלָּתוֹ שֶׁל מָרְדֳּכַי שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ רוֹמֵם אוֹתוֹ – כְּתוּבִים בְּסֵפֶר הַהִסְטוֹרְיָה שֶׁל מַלְכֵי מָדַי וּפָרָס.
verses.english: And, if you are looking for a full account of his might and power, as inspired by Mordechai, and the resultant greatness bestowed upon Mordechai by the king, surely you will find that they are recorded in the Annals of the kings of Media and Persia.

verses.hebrew: שֶׁמָּרְדֳּכַי הַיְּהוּדִי הָיָה מִשְׁנֶה לַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ וְחָשׁוּב בֵּין הַיְּהוּדִים וְרָצוּי לְאֶחָיו הָרַבִּים, מְחַפֵּשׂ לַעֲשׂוֹת טוֹב לְעַמּוֹ וּמְדַבֵּר לְמַעַן שְׁלוֹם כָּל בְּנֵי עַמּוֹ.
verses.english: For Mordechai the Jew remained second in command to King Ahasuerus, enjoying a long tenure. He successfully governed all the empire’s provinces and nations, and of course, the Jews. Although he was faithful to the king’s interests, he was highly regarded by most of his kin, because it was widely recognized that he sought the good of his people and spoke of peace for all its generations.
